pages.summary: Tissues are groups of cells performing a common function, enabling division of labour and organisation from cells to organisms. Two tables compare mitosis with meiosis and plant with animal mitosis. A tree classifies plant tissues into meristematic and permanent tissues and shows their visible subdivisions.

text_image_disagreements.text_says: Cell Tissues Organ Organ system Organisms
text_image_disagreements.image_shows: Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms; the native arrow characters are font-encoding artefacts.

pages.summary: Animal tissues are shown as epithelial, muscular, connective and nervous/neural tissues. The classification tree details epithelial, muscle and connective subtypes; a second illustration links representative tissue appearances with the human body.

Four main body tissues are distinguished by function. Epithelium forms closely packed covering and lining sheets, rests on a basement membrane and may specialise into glands. Six epithelial types are compared by location, structure and function, with four illustrated examples.

p001-i2.content: TISSUE: Cells combine to perform same function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes a group of cells a tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells act together to perform a common function; a mere collection without this functional relationship is not the idea conveyed here.

teacher_understanding.question: Which part of the definition identifies the essential criterion?
teacher_understanding.answer: The phrase 'perform same function' makes shared work the defining link between the cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a shared function useful in a multicellular body?
teacher_understanding.answer: A large body needs reliable protection, transport and movement. Groups of specialised cells can share each job rather than each cell carrying out the body's entire range of tasks.

p001-i2.exam_note: Distinguish tissue from cell, organ and organ system.

terms.plain_meaning: एक जैसा काम मिलकर करने वाली कोशिकाओं का समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक सफाई दल के लोग मिलकर एक काम करते हैं।

why_chain.step: A multicellular body needs different jobs performed efficiently.
Cells combine for the same function, forming a tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue helps produce movement.
unpack.consequence: Introduces the functional unit between cells and organs.
unpack.visual_verb: group cells by their shared job
unpack.level_extra: A tissue need not consist of just one cell type; complex plant tissues later illustrate this.

p001-i3.content: When plant cells combine, they form plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which broad tissue group is formed by plant cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant cells working together constitute plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: What separates this group from the next bullet's group?
teacher_understanding.answer: The organismal source differs: plant cells form plant tissues, whereas animal cells form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'combine' be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It means organised cooperation, not cells melting into one cell. For example, cells in a leaf retain their identities while contributing to the leaf's work.

p001-i3.exam_note: Connects the definition to the plant tissue classification below.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में मिलकर काम करने वाली कोशिकाओं के समूह
terms.everyday_image: पत्ते के भीतर कई कोशिकाएँ मिलकर काम करती हैं।

why_chain.step: A plant needs growth, support and transport.
Its cells organise into tissues to share these jobs.

unpack.example_or_place: The lower chart names xylem and phloem as plant tissues.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the division into meristematic and permanent tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom from a leaf to cooperating cells
unpack.level_extra: Classify by organism first, then by tissue properties.

p001-i4.content: When animal cells combine, they form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cells form animal tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Animal cells organised to work together form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this broad category differ from plant tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells belong to animals rather than plants; both categories still follow the shared-function idea of tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does an animal need tissues rather than independent cells doing unrelated work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Activities such as movement and sensing require coordinated groups of cells; coordination allows the whole animal to respond and function.

p001-i4.exam_note: Foundational distinction for later animal tissue types.

terms.plain_meaning: जानवर के शरीर में मिलकर काम करने वाली कोशिकाओं के समूह
terms.everyday_image: हाथ की मांसपेशी की कोशिकाएँ मिलकर हाथ हिलाती हैं।

why_chain.step: An animal needs coordinated movement and responses.
Groups of specialised cells carry out these shared tasks.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue in the arm.
unpack.consequence: The tissue concept applies to both plants and animals.
unpack.visual_verb: contract a group of muscle cells together
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse an animal tissue with a complete organ such as the heart.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does tissue formation lead to division of labour?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different specialised groups can take responsibility for different body functions instead of each cell performing the entire body's work.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this division operate in a familiar plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells responsible for transport can perform that job while other cells provide support or manufacture food, much as different workers carry out different roles in a workplace.

teacher_understanding.question: What result of tissue formation is explicitly stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies division of labour as a consequence of cells organising into tissues.

p001-i5.exam_note: Reason for tissue-level organisation in multicellular organisms.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग काम अलग समूहों में बाँटना
terms.everyday_image: अस्पताल में डॉक्टर, नर्स और जाँच करने वाले अलग काम सँभालते हैं।

why_chain.step: One cell cannot efficiently do the full range of jobs required by a large organism.
Specialised tissue groups share the work.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: transport tissues and supporting tissues in a plant.
unpack.consequence: Explains reduced workload in the next bullet.
unpack.visual_verb: split tasks among cell groups
unpack.level_extra: Division of labour means functional specialisation, not cell division.

p001-i6.content: Decreases workload on individual cells, hence leads to organisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does tissue organisation reduce an individual cell's workload?
teacher_understanding.answer: A specialised cell concentrates on a limited role while other cells perform complementary roles, so it does not have to perform every function needed by the organism.

teacher_understanding.question: How does shared work produce organisation rather than just a crowd of cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Specialised groups become coordinated and interdependent; their combined work supports larger units such as organs.

teacher_understanding.question: What causal link does the page make?
teacher_understanding.answer: It links reduced workload on individual cells with organisation of the body.

p001-i6.exam_note: Understand the causal connection, not just the phrase.

terms.plain_meaning: काम के अनुसार हिस्सों का व्यवस्थित जुड़ाव
terms.everyday_image: रसोई में कोई सब्जी काटता है और कोई पकाता है, पर भोजन साथ मिलकर बनता है।

why_chain.step: A large body has more tasks than one cell can handle alone.
Sharing tasks reduces individual workload and supports organisation.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: the heart combines several tissues rather than relying on one cell type for every task.
unpack.consequence: Leads directly to the cell-to-organism hierarchy.
unpack.visual_verb: coordinate specialised groups into a larger unit
unpack.level_extra: Specialisation brings interdependence, not independence of tissues.

p001-i7.content: Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms. Each rightward arrow connects a smaller level of biological organisation to the next larger level.

teacher_understanding.question: What hierarchy does the arrow sequence show?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells form tissues, tissues contribute to organs, organs work in organ systems, and systems together make organisms.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does tissue sit in the hierarchy?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is between the individual cell and the organ.

teacher_understanding.question: How can this hierarchy be understood using the human body?
teacher_understanding.answer: A muscle cell belongs to muscle tissue; muscle tissue contributes to the heart; the heart belongs to the circulatory system; that system is part of a person.

terms.plain_meaning: एक बड़ा काम करने वाले अंगों का समूह
terms.everyday_image: मुँह, पेट और आँत भोजन पचाने में साथ काम करते हैं।

why_chain.step: A tissue performs only part of a body's work.
Tissues combine in organs, and organs cooperate in systems.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle cell → muscle tissue → heart → circulatory system → human.
unpack.consequence: Explains how cell-level specialisation supports a whole organism.
unpack.visual_verb: nest smaller units inside larger units
unpack.level_extra: The arrows indicate organisational scale, not a claim that one cell turns into an organ.

p001-i8.content: Cell: first level; arrow points to Tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the starting unit in this hierarchy?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cell is the smallest level shown.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does it connect next?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its arrow leads to tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a cell contribute to a tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: It performs its role in cooperation with neighbouring cells rather than functioning as an isolated miniature organism.

p001-i8.exam_note: First level in the printed sequence.

terms.plain_meaning: जीव की सबसे छोटी जीवित इकाई
terms.everyday_image: दीवार की ईंट जैसी छोटी इकाई, पर यह जीवित है।

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a muscle cell.
unpack.consequence: Cells cooperate to form tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight one cell

p001-i9.content: Tissues: receives the arrow from Cell and points to Organ.

teacher_understanding.question: What unit does this label name?
teacher_understanding.answer: It names the functional groups of cells introduced by the tissue definition.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is tissue located in the sequence?
teacher_understanding.answer: Between cell and organ.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a tissue not the same as an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: An organ generally combines different tissues to carry out a larger task.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue is a component of the heart.
unpack.consequence: The next level combines tissues into an organ.
unpack.visual_verb: bundle cells into a tissue
unpack.level_extra: A tissue is not a complete organ.

p001-i10.content: Organ: receives the arrow from Tissues and points to Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: What is an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a body part in which different tissues cooperate in a particular larger function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the page place an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: After tissues and before organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the heart illustrate this level?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscle produces contraction, while other tissues provide lining, support and coordination, allowing the organ to pump blood.

p001-i10.exam_note: Recognise examples at the organ level.

terms.plain_meaning: कई ऊतकों से बना एक खास काम करने वाला अंग
terms.everyday_image: दिल कई हिस्सों के सहयोग से खून पंप करता है।

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: heart or leaf.
unpack.consequence: Organs cooperate within systems.
unpack.visual_verb: assemble tissues into a heart

p001-i11.content: Organ system: receives the arrow from Organ and points to Organisms.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes an organ system different from a single organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several organs cooperate to carry out a major body function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does it appear in the printed hierarchy?
teacher_understanding.answer: Between organ and organisms.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cooperation among organs necessary?
teacher_understanding.answer: A major function such as digestion requires successive jobs, including food breakdown and nutrient absorption, that different organs perform.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: stomach and intestines in the digestive system.
unpack.consequence: Multiple systems support a whole organism.
unpack.visual_verb: link cooperating organs
unpack.level_extra: Do not use organ and organ system interchangeably.

p001-i12.content: Organisms: final level, receiving the arrow from Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the final label represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: The complete living individual rather than one of its component systems.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is it placed?
teacher_understanding.answer: At the right end of the cell-to-organism sequence.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the whole supported by the earlier levels?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells perform specialised work within tissues, organs and systems whose coordinated activities keep the individual alive.

p001-i12.exam_note: Final level shown, not population or ecosystem.

terms.plain_meaning: पूरे जीवित प्राणी या पौधे
terms.everyday_image: पूरा इंसान, केवल उसका दिल नहीं।

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a person or a mango plant.
unpack.consequence: Completes the levels shown on this page.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom out to a whole organism

p001-i13.content: Comparison table with columns Mitosis and Meiosis and 11 numbered rows: occurrence, nuclear divisions, daughter-cell number, ploidy, frequency, fate, phases, chromosome-number outcome, chromosome doubling, crossing over, and division type.
p001-i13.exam_note: Major comparison; row 9 must not be learned as scientifically correct.

p001-i14.content: 1) Mitosis: It occurs in somatic cells. | Meiosis: It occurs in germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page compare the cells undergoing the two divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: It associates mitosis with somatic cells and meiosis with germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the functional difference between somatic and germ-line cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic cells belong to the non-reproductive body, while germ-line cells are associated with production of reproductive cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do the two cell populations need different division outcomes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Body growth usually requires maintaining chromosome sets; sexual reproduction requires a reduction that prevents chromosome sets doubling at each fertilisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the row mean germ-line cells never undergo mitosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Germ-line precursor cells can multiply by mitosis before some enter meiosis; this row gives the broad contrast, not an exclusive rule.

p001-i14.exam_note: Beware exclusive statements about germ cells and mitosis.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की गैर-प्रजनन कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: त्वचा की मरम्मत करने वाली कोशिकाएँ।

terms.plain_meaning: प्रजनन कोशिकाएँ बनाने वाली कोशिका-वंश की कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: बीज जैसी अगली पीढ़ी की तैयारी करने वाली कोशिकाएँ।

why_chain.step: Bodies need replacement cells, while sexual reproduction needs chromosome reduction.
Mitosis maintains sets; meiosis reduces them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: skin renewal and gamete formation in reproductive organs.
unpack.consequence: Different roles explain later differences in daughter cells.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast body repair with reproductive-cell formation
unpack.level_extra: In flowering plants meiosis produces spores, not directly gametes.

p001-i15.content: 2) Mitosis: Nucleus divides only once. | Meiosis: Nucleus divides twice.

teacher_understanding.question: How many nuclear divisions occur in each?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis has one nuclear division; meiosis has two.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes the two meiotic divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes, while meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are two divisions useful in meiosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: They first reduce chromosome sets and then distribute the chromatids, following only one preceding round of DNA replication.

p001-i15.exam_note: One replication followed by two divisions is the key meiosis distinction.

terms.plain_meaning: कोशिका का वह भाग जिसमें गुणसूत्र रहते हैं
terms.everyday_image: जरूरी निर्देशों का सुरक्षित रिकॉर्ड-कक्ष।

why_chain.step: Reproductive cells need a reduced chromosome set.
Meiosis separates homologues and then chromatids in two divisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: meiosis during sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Explains the two-versus-four daughter-cell outcome.
unpack.visual_verb: split once versus split twice
unpack.level_extra: Two divisions do not imply two DNA-replication rounds.

p001-i16.content: 3) Mitosis: Two daughter cells are formed. | Meiosis: Four daughter cells are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: What daughter-cell numbers are stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table gives two products for mitosis and four for meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What division pattern accounts for the numerical difference?
teacher_understanding.answer: One mitotic division gives two cells, while two successive meiotic divisions produce four cellular products in the standard scheme.

teacher_understanding.question: Should four meiotic products be understood as four equally functional gametes?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. In human egg formation, unequal divisions yield one large functional ovum and polar bodies, unlike the four functional sperm typically produced from one primary spermatocyte.

p001-i16.exam_note: Distinguish meiotic products from functional gametes.

terms.plain_meaning: विभाजन से बनी नई कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: एक कमरे को बाँटकर बने नए कमरे।

why_chain.step: One division separates one cell into two products.
A further division of the two meiotic products gives four.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Cell count must be considered separately from chromosome count.
unpack.visual_verb: branch one cell into two and then four
unpack.level_extra: Four products need not mean four viable gametes.

p001-i17.content: 4) Mitosis: Daughter cells are diploid. | Meiosis: Daughter cells are haploid.

teacher_understanding.question: What ploidy contrast does the table state?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes mitotic daughters as diploid and meiotic daughters as haploid.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between diploid and haploid?
teacher_understanding.answer: Diploid means two chromosome sets, written 2n; haploid means one set, written n. Here n denotes one complete chromosome set, not a unit of measurement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should the mitosis statement be qualified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis normally preserves the parent's ploidy. A diploid parent gives diploid daughters, but a haploid cell can also undergo mitosis and remain haploid.

p001-i17.exam_note: Trap: mitosis is not intrinsically restricted to diploid cells.

terms.plain_meaning: गुणसूत्रों के दो पूरे सेट
terms.everyday_image: एक ही किताब के दो पूरे सेट।

terms.plain_meaning: गुणसूत्रों का एक पूरा सेट
terms.everyday_image: किताबों का एक पूरा सेट, आधी-अधूरी किताबें नहीं।

why_chain.step: Fertilisation brings together chromosome sets from two gametes.
Meiosis reduces the sets before fertilisation restores the diploid state.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: human body cells are generally diploid; gametes are haploid.
unpack.consequence: Sets, rather than DNA quantity alone, define ploidy.
unpack.visual_verb: compare two chromosome sets with one
unpack.level_extra: Mitosis preserves ploidy; do not memorise diploid daughters as an unconditional rule.

p001-i18.content: 5) Mitosis: It occurs more frequently. | Meiosis: It occurs less frequently.

teacher_understanding.question: What frequency comparison is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis is described as more frequent and meiosis as less frequent.

teacher_understanding.question: How do their biological demands differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Growth and repair require repeated cell production across many tissues, whereas meiosis is restricted to particular reproductive stages and cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this not a universal numerical law?
teacher_understanding.answer: Frequency depends on the organism, tissue, age and reproductive cycle; the row gives a broad functional comparison rather than a fixed rate.

p001-i18.exam_note: Qualitative statement, not a measured ratio.

why_chain.step: Body maintenance needs repeated replacement cells.
Mitosis therefore has broader routine roles than meiosis.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: regular replacement of intestinal lining cells.
unpack.consequence: Frequency reflects biological role.
unpack.visual_verb: repeat body-cell divisions beside a restricted reproductive event
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that every somatic cell divides frequently.

p001-i19.content: 6) Mitosis: Daughter cells form somatic organs. | Meiosis: Daughter cells form gametes.

teacher_understanding.question: What fates are assigned to the daughter cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitotic daughters contribute to somatic organs; meiotic daughters are associated with gamete formation.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these outcomes serve different needs?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic growth builds and maintains an individual; gametes contribute genetic material to a new individual through fertilisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must the gamete claim be qualified in plants?
teacher_understanding.answer: In flowering plants, meiosis produces haploid spores; gametes develop later through the gametophyte stage and mitotic divisions. The printed row is a simplified animal-centred contrast.

p001-i19.exam_note: Do not generalise direct gamete production by meiosis to all life cycles.

terms.plain_meaning: निषेचन में मिलने वाली प्रजनन कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: शुक्राणु और अंडाणु मिलकर नई शुरुआत करते हैं।

why_chain.step: An individual needs body maintenance and a way to reproduce.
Mitotic growth and the meiotic reproductive pathway serve these distinct needs.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: skin repair and sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Links cell division to tissue growth and reproduction.
unpack.visual_verb: route daughter cells toward body tissue or reproduction
unpack.level_extra: Plant spore formation is the important qualification.

p001-i20.content: 7) Mitosis: There is only one prophase, one metaphase one anaphase and one telophase. | Meiosis: There are two of each phase and five sub-phases in prophase - 1.

teacher_understanding.question: How are the named phases distributed across the two divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis has one sequence of prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Meiosis has two sequences and five subdivisions within prophase I.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes prophase I especially different?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologous chromosomes pair and exchange segments, requiring more elaborate events than the usual mitotic prophase.

teacher_understanding.question: How can the phase names be understood rather than memorised as a list?
teacher_understanding.answer: Chromosomes prepare and condense in prophase, line up in metaphase, separate in anaphase, and reach the poles as nuclei reorganise in telophase.

teacher_understanding.question: What are the standard names of the five prophase I subdivisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis; these names are explanatory additions, not labels printed on this page.

p001-i20.exam_note: Prophase I and crossing over are key comparison points.

terms.plain_meaning: विभाजन का शुरुआती चरण, जिसमें गुणसूत्र साफ दिखने लगते हैं
terms.everyday_image: काम शुरू होने से पहले सामान व्यवस्थित करना।

terms.plain_meaning: एक बड़े चरण के भीतर छोटे चरण
terms.everyday_image: खाना पकाने में तैयारी के भीतर धोना, काटना और मसाला लगाना।

why_chain.step: Chromosomes must be organised before they can separate safely.
Meiosis I adds pairing and exchange, making its prophase more elaborate.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: chromosome pairing in a meiotic reproductive cell.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the crossing-over comparison.
unpack.visual_verb: prepare, align, separate and regroup chromosomes
unpack.level_extra: Two phase sequences do not mean DNA replicates between them.

p001-i21.content: 8) Mitosis: Number of chromosomes are not changed in the daughter cells. | Meiosis: Number of chromosomes are reduced to half.

teacher_understanding.question: How does daughter-cell chromosome number compare with the parent?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is maintained in mitosis and reduced to half in meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: Which chromosome separation creates the reduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I; mitosis instead distributes sister chromatids so daughters retain the parent's chromosome-set number.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is halving essential for sexual reproduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: Two gametes later fuse. Halving before fusion allows the usual chromosome-set number to be restored instead of doubling each generation.

terms.plain_meaning: वंशानुगत सूचना रखने वाली DNA की व्यवस्थित संरचनाएँ
terms.everyday_image: शरीर बनाने के निर्देशों की किताबें।

why_chain.step: Fertilisation combines two chromosome sets.
Meiosis halves the parental number before that combination.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: human diploid cells generally have 46 chromosomes and gametes 23.
unpack.consequence: Explains equational and reduction division in row 11.
unpack.visual_verb: preserve one count and halve the other
unpack.level_extra: Separate chromosome number from DNA content.

p001-i22.content: 9) Mitosis: Chromosome number doubles at the beginning of each cell division. | Meiosis: Chromosome number is not doubled. It doubles after the end of first meiotic division.

teacher_understanding.question: What chromosome-doubling claims are printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The mitosis cell claims chromosome number doubles at the start of each division; the meiosis cell says it is not doubled and then says it doubles after the first meiotic division.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the correct distinction between chromosome number and DNA replication?
teacher_understanding.answer: DNA replicates before mitosis and before meiosis I. Replication produces sister chromatids without doubling the chromosome number as counted by centromeres. There is no intervening DNA replication between meiosis I and meiosis II.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the printed row unsafe to memorise?
teacher_understanding.answer: It confuses DNA amount with chromosome number and incorrectly places a doubling after meiosis I. These errors obscure the one-replication, two-division basis of meiosis.

p001-i22.exam_note: Scientific error in source: use the explicitly separated correction, not the printed claim.

terms.plain_meaning: गुणसूत्रों की गिनती, केवल DNA की मात्रा नहीं
terms.everyday_image: किताब की एक फोटोकॉपी उससे लगी हो तो सामग्री बढ़ती है, पर मूल पहचान की गिनती अलग रहती है।

why_chain.step: Daughter cells need a supply of genetic material before division.
DNA is copied before mitosis or meiosis I, not between the two meiotic divisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside illustration: a replicated chromosome has two sister chromatids joined at a centromere.
unpack.consequence: Prevents a false explanation of chromosome reduction.
unpack.visual_verb: copy chromatids while keeping chromosome identity marked
unpack.level_extra: Flag the row as erroneous; DNA content and chromosome count are not interchangeable.

p001-i23.content: 10) Mitosis: No crossing over in chromosomes. | Meiosis: Crossing over occurs chromosomes [occurs in chromosomes].

teacher_understanding.question: How does the table contrast crossing over?
teacher_understanding.answer: It presents crossing over as absent in mitosis and present in meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What does crossing over add to meiotic products?
teacher_understanding.answer: Exchange between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes produces new combinations of inherited genetic material.

teacher_understanding.question: How and when does the standard meiotic exchange occur?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologous chromosomes pair during prophase I, and exchange occurs during pachytene. This is the ordinary textbook contrast with mitosis; rare mitotic recombination is outside that simplified comparison.

p001-i23.exam_note: Crossing over: meiosis I, genetic recombination.

terms.plain_meaning: मिलते-जुलते गुणसूत्रों के बीच DNA के टुकड़ों का आदान-प्रदान
terms.everyday_image: दो रंगीन फीते अपने बराबर हिस्से बदल लें।

why_chain.step: Sexual reproduction generates varied combinations of inherited information.
Paired homologues exchange matching segments during meiosis I.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: new combinations of maternal and paternal chromosome segments in gametes.
unpack.consequence: Meiotic products are not generally genetically identical.
unpack.visual_verb: exchange coloured chromosome segments
unpack.level_extra: Crossing over is between non-sister chromatids, not simply any two chromosomes.

p001-i24.content: 11) Mitosis: Equation [Equational] division. | Meiosis: Reduction division.

teacher_understanding.question: What division names are contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The row calls mitosis 'Equation division' and meiosis 'Reduction division'.

teacher_understanding.question: What do equational and reduction division mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: Equational division maintains chromosome-set number; reduction division halves it.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the meiosis label more precisely attached to meiosis I?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologues separate and chromosome sets are reduced in meiosis I. Meiosis II separates sister chromatids and is equational.

p001-i24.exam_note: Meiosis I is reductional; meiosis II is equational.

terms.plain_meaning: गुणसूत्रों के सेट आधे करने वाला विभाजन
terms.everyday_image: दो पूरे सेटों में से एक-एक सेट अलग समूह को देना।

why_chain.step: Sexual reproduction needs chromosome reduction before fusion.
Meiosis I performs the reduction; mitosis preserves the set number.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: diploid meiotic precursor producing haploid products.
unpack.consequence: Summarises the chromosome-number comparison.
unpack.visual_verb: label preserved versus halved chromosome sets
unpack.level_extra: The printed word 'Equation' is corrected explicitly, not silently.

p001-i25.content: Table 7.3: Difference between mitosis in Plants and Animals. Columns: Plants | Animals. Four rows compare centrioles, asters, cytokinesis and sites of occurrence.
p001-i25.exam_note: Read as the standard higher-plant versus animal-cell comparison.

p001-i26.content: Plants: Centrioles are absent. | Animals: Centrioles are present.

teacher_understanding.question: What centriole contrast is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table describes plant cells as lacking centrioles and animal cells as possessing them.

teacher_understanding.question: Does absence of centrioles mean plant cells cannot form a spindle?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Typical higher-plant cells organise spindle microtubules without the centriole-containing centrosomes typical of animal cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the scope of this comparison be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the standard comparison of higher-plant cells with typical animal cells, not a universal claim about every cell in every plant or animal lineage.

p001-i26.exam_note: Centriole absence does not imply spindle absence.

terms.plain_meaning: सूक्ष्म नलिकाओं से बनी छोटी बेलनाकार कोशिकीय संरचनाएँ
terms.everyday_image: छोटे खोखले बेलन जैसी बनावट।

why_chain.step: Chromosomes need a spindle for organised separation.
Plant and animal cells organise this machinery differently.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside comparison: dividing root-tip cell and typical animal cell.
unpack.consequence: Links to the aster comparison below.
unpack.visual_verb: show centrioles at animal spindle poles and omit them in the plant cell
unpack.level_extra: Qualify the broad plant–animal wording.

p001-i27.content: Plants: Asters are not formed. | Animals: Asters are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: How does aster formation differ in the table?
teacher_understanding.answer: Asters are shown as absent in plants and present in animals.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes an aster from the spindle as a whole?
teacher_understanding.answer: An aster is a star-like array of microtubules radiating around a spindle pole; it is not the entire chromosome-separating spindle.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does this row accompany the centriole row?
teacher_understanding.answer: Typical animal centrosomes organise astral microtubules, whereas higher-plant mitotic spindles generally lack those conspicuous astral arrays.

p001-i27.exam_note: Plant division is commonly termed anastral, animal division astral.

terms.plain_meaning: विभाजन के ध्रुवों के पास तारे जैसी फैली सूक्ष्म नलिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: तारे से चारों ओर निकलती किरणें।

why_chain.step: The division apparatus needs spatial organisation.
Typical animal poles have radiating astral arrays; higher-plant poles generally do not.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: star-like arrays at poles of a typical dividing animal cell.
unpack.consequence: Provides a visual identification feature.
unpack.visual_verb: radiate fibres from a spindle pole
unpack.level_extra: No aster does not mean no spindle.

p001-i28.content: Plants: Cell division involves formation of a cell plate. | Animals: Cell division involves furrowing and cleavage of cytoplasm.

teacher_understanding.question: How does cytoplasmic division differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plants form a cell plate, while animals divide by furrowing and cleavage of the cytoplasm.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the directional difference between these mechanisms?
teacher_understanding.answer: A plant cell plate develops near the centre and expands outward; the animal cleavage furrow constricts inward from the surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the plant use a plate rather than the usual animal pinching mechanism?
teacher_understanding.answer: A rigid cell wall resists pinching. Building a new partition inside the cell separates the daughters while allowing a new wall to develop.

p001-i28.exam_note: Cell plate versus cleavage furrow is a frequent statement-based distinction.

terms.plain_meaning: पौध कोशिका के बीच बनने वाला नया विभाजक
terms.everyday_image: एक कमरे के बीच नई दीवार बनाना।

terms.plain_meaning: बाहर से अंदर की ओर खाँच बनाकर कसना
terms.everyday_image: थैली को बीच से डोरी से कसना।

why_chain.step: Two daughter nuclei need separate cytoplasmic compartments.
A rigid plant wall favours internal partition building; an animal cell can constrict.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside comparison: onion root-tip cytokinesis and animal-cell cytokinesis.
unpack.consequence: Separates cytokinesis from nuclear division.
unpack.visual_verb: grow a central plate versus pinch inward
unpack.level_extra: Mitosis concerns nuclear division; this row describes associated cytokinesis.

p001-i29.content: Plants: Occurs mainly at meristem. | Animals: Occurs in tissues throughout the body.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the table locate plant and animal mitosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant mitosis occurs mainly in meristems; animal mitosis occurs in tissues distributed through the body.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this reflect their growth patterns?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant growth is concentrated in specialised growing regions, whereas many animal tissues retain local cell populations for growth or replacement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'throughout the body' not the same as 'in every animal cell'?
teacher_understanding.answer: Many mature specialised cells divide little or not at all; division is concentrated in cells capable of renewal within particular tissues.

p001-i29.exam_note: Notice 'mainly'; neither column means every cell divides.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे का सक्रिय रूप से नई कोशिकाएँ बनाने वाला क्षेत्र
terms.everyday_image: नई शाखा की बढ़ती नोक।

why_chain.step: Plants need continuing growth at selected regions.
Meristems supply new cells at those regions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: root tip in plants and skin renewal in animals.
unpack.consequence: Bridges the division table to meristematic tissue in the chart.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight plant growth zones and scattered animal renewal sites
unpack.level_extra: Mature neurons and many muscle cells challenge an overbroad reading.

p001-i30.content: Classification of Plant Tissue. Root branches to Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue. Meristematic Tissue branches to Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem. Permanent Tissue branches to Simple and Complex. Simple branches to Paranchyma [Parenchyma], Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma. Sclerenchyma branches to Fibres and Sclereids. Complex branches to Xylem and Phloem. Visible Xylem components are Tracheids, Vessels (Tracheae) and Xylem parenchyma. Visible Phloem components are Sieve tubes, Companion cells and Phloem parenchyma. The component boxes end at the bottom edge of the graphic.

teacher_understanding.question: What are the chart's main branches and subdivisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant tissues divide into meristematic and permanent tissues. Meristematic tissues have apical, lateral and intercalary branches. Permanent tissues divide into simple and complex; simple includes parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma, while complex includes xylem and phloem. Sclerenchyma divides into fibres and sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: What bases distinguish the first two branching levels?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic versus permanent distinguishes actively dividing tissue from differentiated tissue. Simple versus complex distinguishes tissue mainly of one cell type from tissue composed of different cell types working together.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are xylem and phloem not additional branches beside simple and complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are examples within the complex permanent-tissue category. Reading the connecting lines preserves category levels and prevents mixing a class with its members.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the lowest boxes be read?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their listed names are components of xylem or phloem, not additional tissue categories parallel to meristematic and permanent tissue.

p001-i30.exam_note: High-yield hierarchy for matching, odd-one-out and correct-statement questions.

terms.plain_meaning: किसी आधार पर चीजों को समूहों और उपसमूहों में बाँटना
terms.everyday_image: अलमारी में पहले कपड़े और किताबें, फिर कपड़ों में शर्ट और पैंट अलग करना।

why_chain.step: A plant needs both new cells and cells specialised for particular jobs.
The hierarchy separates growth tissues from permanent tissues and then subdivides them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: root tips illustrate growth tissue; a stem's vascular bundles illustrate complex permanent tissue.
unpack.consequence: Provides the map for subsequent plant tissue lessons.
unpack.visual_verb: branch categories and trace each leaf to its parent
unpack.level_extra: The cropped component lists are not an exhaustive inventory; standard xylem and phloem classifications also include fibres.

p001-i31.content: Classification of Plant Tissue: root label; branches to Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two groups descend directly from the root?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic tissue and permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What separates the two groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: Active cell division characterises meristematic tissue; permanent tissue is differentiated for particular functions and generally has lost routine division capacity.

teacher_understanding.question: Why begin with this split?
teacher_understanding.answer: A plant needs both a supply of new cells and mature cells that perform support, storage and transport.

why_chain.step: Growth and specialised work are different needs.
The first split separates the tissues serving these broad roles.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: growing root tip versus mature conducting tissue.
unpack.consequence: Every lower label belongs under one of these two groups.
unpack.visual_verb: split the root into two main branches

p001-i32.content: Meristematic Tissue: child of Classification of Plant Tissue; parent of Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three types are grouped under meristematic tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical, lateral and intercalary meristems.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this group differ from permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: It retains active division to supply new cells, unlike generally differentiated permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must plants retain such tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Continued growth requires a source of new cells at growing regions.

p001-i32.exam_note: Meristem types are classified by position.

terms.plain_meaning: लगातार विभाजन करके नई कोशिकाएँ देने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: निर्माण स्थल पर नई ईंटें पहुँचाने वाली इकाई।

why_chain.step: Plant growth needs new cells.
Meristematic cells divide to provide them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: root and shoot tips.
unpack.consequence: Its three positional types explain different directions of growth.
unpack.visual_verb: multiply cells in growing zones
unpack.level_extra: Meristem is not a transport tissue.

p001-i33.content: Apical Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The chart places it under meristematic tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How is apical meristem distinguished from lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristem is at root and shoot tips and contributes to lengthening; lateral meristem contributes mainly to thickening.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a tip produce length growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Division supplies new cells behind the tip; subsequent enlargement and differentiation extend the root or shoot.

p001-i33.exam_note: Tip location and primary length growth.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ या तने की नोक का बढ़ने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: पौधे की आगे बढ़ती नोक।

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots need to extend into new space.
Tip meristems supply cells for this extension.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a growing root tip.
unpack.consequence: Increases length rather than primarily girth.
unpack.visual_verb: extend a root and shoot at their tips
unpack.level_extra: Apical means at the apex or tip.

p001-i34.content: Lateral Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main tissue group contains lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does lateral growth differ from apical growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems increase stem or root girth; apical meristems primarily contribute to length.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a growing woody stem need lateral meristems?
teacher_understanding.answer: As the plant becomes larger, additional supporting and conducting tissues are needed; lateral meristems add tissues that thicken the stem.

terms.plain_meaning: तने या जड़ की मोटाई बढ़ाने वाला किनारे का विभाजी ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: पेड़ का तना साल-दर-साल मोटा होना।

why_chain.step: A larger plant needs more support and conducting tissue.
Lateral meristems add tissue and increase girth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular cambium in a woody stem.
unpack.consequence: Explains thickening, not merely height increase.
unpack.visual_verb: expand a stem outward in rings
unpack.level_extra: Secondary growth is not equally developed in every plant group.

p001-i35.content: Intercalary Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue group includes intercalary meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is one of the three meristematic tissue types shown.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its position differ from apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It lies between more mature tissues, often near leaf or internode bases in grasses, rather than solely at the root or shoot apex.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it help grass regrow after cutting?
teacher_understanding.answer: Basal growing regions can remain intact after upper parts are removed and supply new cells for renewed elongation.

terms.plain_meaning: परिपक्व ऊतकों के बीच बचा हुआ बढ़ने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: ऊपर से कटने पर भी घास नीचे से फिर बढ़ती है।

why_chain.step: Grasses need elongation even when upper parts are removed.
Growing regions near the base can continue supplying cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: grass leaf bases.
unpack.consequence: Growth can occur away from the terminal apex.
unpack.visual_verb: regrow grass from an intact base
unpack.level_extra: Intercalary means inserted between other regions.

p001-i36.content: Permanent Tissue: child of Classification of Plant Tissue; parent of Simple and Complex.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two groups descend from permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple and complex tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How does permanent tissue differ from meristematic tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells are differentiated for particular jobs and generally no longer divide routinely.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'permanent' not equivalent to 'dead'?
teacher_understanding.answer: Differentiation concerns specialisation and division capacity; many permanent tissues contain living cells, including parenchyma and much of phloem.

p001-i36.exam_note: Permanent tissue includes living and dead cell types.

terms.plain_meaning: विशेष काम के लिए परिपक्व हुआ ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: प्रशिक्षण के बाद तय जिम्मेदारी निभाने वाला कर्मचारी।

why_chain.step: A plant needs cells to perform stable specialised jobs.
Cells differentiate into permanent tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: storage parenchyma in a potato.
unpack.consequence: Further divides by cell-type composition into simple and complex.
unpack.visual_verb: differentiate new cells into specialised workers
unpack.level_extra: Permanent does not mean incapable of division under every possible condition.

p001-i37.content: Simple: child of Permanent Tissue; parent of Paranchyma [Parenchyma], Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which simple tissues are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes simple from complex permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple tissue is composed mainly of similar cells; complex tissue contains different cell types cooperating in a common function.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does 'simple' not mean unimportant or functionless?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes cell-type composition, not importance; these tissues can store food, photosynthesise or support the plant.

p001-i37.exam_note: Odd-one-out: xylem and phloem are not simple tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्य रूप से एक जैसे प्रकार की कोशिकाओं वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: एक ही तरह के कामगारों की टोली।

why_chain.step: Some plant tasks can be performed by similar cells grouped together.
These form the simple permanent-tissue category.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: storage tissue in fleshy plant parts.
unpack.consequence: Contains three named tissue types in the chart.
unpack.visual_verb: group similar cells under one branch
unpack.level_extra: Simple versus complex is not a living-versus-dead distinction.

p001-i38.content: Complex: child of Permanent Tissue; parent of Xylem and Phloem. Its connecting line descends to the two lower component boxes.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissues are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes them complex rather than simple?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each combines several cell types that cooperate, especially in transport.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does transport require more than one kind of cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: Conducting elements need associated cells for support, storage or maintenance, so the tissue operates as a coordinated team.

p001-i38.exam_note: Both vascular tissues are complex permanent tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: कई प्रकार की कोशिकाओं का मिलकर बना ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: ड्राइवर, मरम्मत कर्मचारी और प्रबंधक मिलकर बस सेवा चलाते हैं।

why_chain.step: Transport needs conducting pathways plus support and maintenance.
Different cell types cooperate in xylem and phloem.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular bundles in a stem.
unpack.consequence: The bottom boxes list component cells, not separate main classes.
unpack.visual_verb: combine different cell types into one transport team
unpack.level_extra: Complex does not mean made only of dead cells.

p001-i39.content: Paranchyma [Parenchyma]: child of Simple, under Permanent Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: The chart places it under simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does parenchyma broadly differ from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma generally has living, relatively thin-walled cells; typical mature sclerenchyma provides stronger support through thick lignified walls and usually dead cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How does parenchyma relate to familiar food?
teacher_understanding.answer: Living storage cells in fleshy plant parts can accumulate food and water; potato tissue is a familiar storage example.

p001-i39.exam_note: Correct spelling is Parenchyma; printed spelling retained explicitly.

terms.plain_meaning: आमतौर पर पतली भित्ति वाली जीवित कोशिकाओं का सरल ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: आलू का भोजन जमा करने वाला गूदा।

why_chain.step: Plants need storage and other everyday metabolic work.
Living parenchyma cells can perform such functions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: potato storage tissue.
unpack.consequence: One of three simple tissue types, but parenchyma also occurs as a component of complex tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: fill thin-walled cells with stored food
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish parenchyma as a tissue from xylem or phloem parenchyma as a component.

p001-i40.content: Collenchyma: child of Simple, under Permanent Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is collenchyma classified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Under simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from typical sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collenchyma has living cells with unevenly thickened walls and gives flexible support; sclerenchyma typically has thick lignified walls and provides more rigid support.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful to a young plant part?
teacher_understanding.answer: A growing shoot or leaf stalk must resist bending forces while still extending and moving without easily breaking.

p001-i40.exam_note: Flexible support, living cells, uneven wall thickening.

terms.plain_meaning: जीवित कोशिकाओं वाला लचीला सहारा देने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: नरम डंडी हवा में झुकती है, तुरंत टूटती नहीं।

why_chain.step: Young plant parts need support without preventing growth.
Unevenly thickened living cells provide flexible strength.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: beneath the epidermis of many young dicot stems and leaf stalks.
unpack.consequence: Provides a contrast with rigid sclerenchyma.
unpack.visual_verb: bend a supported young stalk
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse collenchyma with chlorenchyma.

p001-i41.content: Sclerenchyma: child of Simple, under Permanent Tissue; parent of Fibres and Sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two subdivisions belong to sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres and sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: How does sclerenchyma differ from parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: It typically consists of thick, lignified supporting cells that are dead at maturity, rather than the living thin-walled cells typical of parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can dead cells still support a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their hardened walls remain after the living contents disappear, so mechanical strength does not require a living protoplast.

p001-i41.exam_note: Support tissue; distinguish fibres and sclereids.

terms.plain_meaning: कठोर मोटी भित्तियों से मजबूत सहारा देने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: नारियल के कठोर और रेशेदार हिस्सों का सहारा।

why_chain.step: Mature plant parts need mechanical strength.
Thick lignified walls provide support even when the cells are dead.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: coconut fibres and hard seed coats.
unpack.consequence: Branches into elongated fibres and varied sclereids.
unpack.visual_verb: thicken and harden cell walls
unpack.level_extra: Cell death does not eliminate the supporting function of the wall.

p001-i42.where_on_page: chart, left yellow box below Sclerenchyma

teacher_understanding.question: Which simple tissue contains the fibres branch?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibres broadly differ from sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres are characteristically long and narrow with thick walls; sclereids are commonly shorter or irregularly shaped.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the long shape useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long cells arranged in bundles can resist pulling forces and strengthen plant parts like a set of reinforcing strands.

p001-i42.exam_note: Fibre versus sclereid shape and examples.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबी, पतली और मजबूत मोटी भित्ति वाली कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी के लंबे मजबूत रेशे।

why_chain.step: Plant parts must resist pulling and bending.
Bundles of elongated thick-walled cells reinforce them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: jute fibres.
unpack.consequence: One structural form of sclerenchyma.
unpack.visual_verb: bundle elongated cells like reinforcing strands
unpack.level_extra: Fibres can also be components of vascular tissues; the chart's bottom lists are cropped.

p001-i43.where_on_page: chart, right yellow box below Sclerenchyma

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How are sclereids distinguished from fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclereids have varied shapes and are often short or stone-like rather than uniformly long and narrow.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a learner recognise their effect in food?
teacher_understanding.answer: Clusters of hard sclereids contribute to the gritty texture felt when eating a pear.

p001-i43.exam_note: Pear grit and hard shells are useful recognition links.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग आकार की कठोर, मोटी भित्ति वाली कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: नाशपाती खाते समय महसूस होने वाले छोटे कड़े कण।

why_chain.step: Some plant parts need local hardness or protection.
Thick-walled sclereids provide that hardness.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: pear pulp and hard seed coverings.
unpack.consequence: Completes the sclerenchyma subdivision.
unpack.visual_verb: embed hard cells in soft fruit tissue
unpack.level_extra: Sclereids are also called stone cells in common textbook usage.

p001-i44.where_on_page: chart, lower left component box heading
p001-i44.content: Xylem: child of Complex, under Permanent Tissue; visible components are Tracheids, Vessels (Tracheae) and Xylem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible components are listed under xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids, vessels or tracheae, and xylem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does xylem's main transport role differ from phloem's?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly conducts water and dissolved minerals; phloem transports organic food substances from sources to sinks.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is xylem classified as complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different component cells contribute conduction, storage and support rather than one uniform cell type performing all roles.

p001-i44.exam_note: Xylem is not wholly dead: xylem parenchyma is living.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और घुले खनिज पहुँचाने वाला जटिल ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: जड़ों से पत्तों तक पानी की पाइपलाइन।

why_chain.step: Leaves need water absorbed by roots.
Xylem provides conducting pathways with associated supporting and storage cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: xylem in a stem's vascular bundles.
unpack.consequence: Its separate component labels explain why it is complex.
unpack.visual_verb: carry water through a multicellular pathway
unpack.level_extra: Standard xylem also includes xylem fibres, not visible in this crop.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue includes tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do tracheids differ from vessel elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids are elongated, tapering cells with intact end walls; water passes through pits. Vessel elements join through perforated end regions to form more continuous tubes.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a dead tracheid conduct water?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its mature hollow interior and pits provide a pathway, while its lignified walls resist collapse.

p001-i45.exam_note: Dead at maturity; conducting and supporting role.

terms.plain_meaning: सिरों पर पतली होती लंबी जलवाहक कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: नुकीले सिरों वाली बंद नलियाँ, जिनकी दीवारों के रास्ते पानी आगे जाता है।

why_chain.step: Water needs a continuous route through successive cells.
Tracheid pits permit passage between neighbouring hollow cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: an important conducting element in conifer wood.
unpack.consequence: One of xylem's conducting cell types.
unpack.visual_verb: pass water through pits between tapered cells
unpack.level_extra: Do not place tracheids under phloem.

p001-i46.content: Vessels (Tracheae): listed component of Xylem; Tracheae is the alternative name printed in parentheses.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains vessels, also called tracheae here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a vessel differ from a single tracheid?
teacher_understanding.answer: A vessel is a tube formed by vessel elements joined end to end with perforated end regions, whereas a tracheid remains an individual tapering cell with unperforated end walls.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are joined vessel elements effective in transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their open connections provide a relatively continuous route for water through the tissue.

p001-i46.exam_note: Plant tracheae here means vessels, not insect respiratory tubes.

terms.plain_meaning: सिरे से सिरे जुड़कर बनी जलवाहक नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: कई छोटे पाइप जोड़कर बनी लंबी पाइपलाइन।

why_chain.step: Water must travel across many cells.
Perforated connections join vessel elements into conducting tubes.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vessel elements in wood of many flowering plants.
unpack.consequence: Adds another conducting element to xylem.
unpack.visual_verb: join hollow elements end to end
unpack.level_extra: The same word can have different meanings in plant and animal contexts.

p001-i47.where_on_page: chart, Xylem box, lowest visible component
p001-i47.content: Xylem parenchyma: listed component of Xylem; last visible label before the graphic ends.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains this parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from mature tracheids and vessel elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem parenchyma cells are living and contribute storage and short-distance transport; mature conducting tracheids and vessel elements are dead.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does its presence matter in classification questions?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows that xylem cannot correctly be described as composed exclusively of dead cells.

p001-i47.exam_note: Living component of xylem is a common statement trap.

terms.plain_meaning: जाइलम में मौजूद जीवित संग्रह और सहायक परिवहन कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: पाइपलाइन के पास सामान रखने और सँभालने वाला कमरा।

why_chain.step: A transport tissue needs storage and lateral exchange as well as long-distance conduction.
Living parenchyma cells provide associated functions in xylem.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: living parenchyma in wood, including radial pathways.
unpack.consequence: Confirms mixed cell types within complex tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: store material beside conducting tubes
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer all xylem cells are dead.

p001-i48.where_on_page: chart, lower right component box heading
p001-i48.content: Phloem: child of Complex, under Permanent Tissue; visible components are Sieve tubes, Companion cells and Phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible components belong to phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its main transport cargo differ from xylem's?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem moves organic nutrients, especially sugars, from sources to sinks; xylem mainly transports water and minerals.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need this second transport tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Photosynthetic leaves make food, but roots, growing parts and storage organs also need it, so nutrients must be distributed beyond their production sites.

p001-i48.exam_note: Food transport; avoid saying phloem flow is simply downward in every case.

terms.plain_meaning: शर्करा जैसे बने हुए भोजन को जरूरत की जगह पहुँचाने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: रसोई से अलग-अलग कमरों तक खाना पहुँचाने की सेवा।

why_chain.step: Roots and growing tissues need food made elsewhere.
Phloem distributes organic nutrients from sources to sinks.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: sugar moving from leaves to growing roots or fruits.
unpack.consequence: Its cell team is unpacked in the next three labels.
unpack.visual_verb: send sugar from leaves to growing and storage regions
unpack.level_extra: Standard phloem classification also includes phloem fibres, not visible in this crop.

p001-i49.content: Sieve tubes: listed component of Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains sieve tubes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do sieve-tube elements differ from xylem vessel elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve-tube elements are living conducting cells with perforated sieve plates and reduced internal contents; mature xylem vessel elements are dead and hollow.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the sieve-like arrangement support transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pores in the end plates permit phloem sap to move between successive tube elements.

p001-i49.exam_note: Living at maturity but mature sieve-tube elements lack a nucleus.

terms.plain_meaning: छिद्रदार अंतिम प्लेटों से जुड़ी भोजन-वाहक कोशिकाओं की नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: छलनी जैसी जाली वाले जोड़ से गुजरता तरल।

why_chain.step: Sugar-rich sap must pass along successive living conducting cells.
Sieve plates provide connecting pores between them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: phloem of a flowering-plant stem.
unpack.consequence: Their reduced cell machinery helps explain the association with companion cells.
unpack.visual_verb: pass sap through perforated end plates
unpack.level_extra: A living cell can lack a nucleus at maturity; do not confuse nucleus absence with death.

p001-i50.content: Companion cells: listed component of Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains companion cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do companion cells differ from sieve-tube elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Companion cells retain a nucleus and dense living contents, while mature sieve-tube elements have greatly reduced contents and lack a nucleus.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are companion cells associated with sieve tubes?
teacher_understanding.answer: They provide metabolic support and help regulate loading and unloading, allowing reduced sieve-tube elements to specialise in transport.

p001-i50.exam_note: Companion cells support sieve tubes, not xylem vessels.

terms.plain_meaning: चालनी नलिकाओं को कामकाज में मदद देने वाली जीवित कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: वाहन चलाने वाले के साथ व्यवस्था सँभालने वाला सहायक।

why_chain.step: Reduced sieve-tube elements cannot independently perform the full range of cellular maintenance.
Connected companion cells provide metabolic assistance.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: companion cells beside sieve-tube elements in flowering plants.
unpack.consequence: Illustrates division of labour within one complex tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: support a conducting cell from an adjacent nucleated cell
unpack.level_extra: Connects the opening division-of-labour idea to a specific tissue team.

p001-i51.where_on_page: chart, Phloem box, lowest visible component
p001-i51.content: Phloem parenchyma: listed component of Phloem; last visible label before the graphic ends.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains phloem parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its role differ from that of sieve tubes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem parenchyma contributes storage and short-distance exchange, whereas sieve tubes are the principal long-distance conducting elements in flowering-plant phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can parenchyma appear in both the simple-tissue branch and complex-tissue boxes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma describes a cell and tissue type that can form tissue by itself or occur as one component in a larger mixed tissue such as xylem or phloem.

p001-i51.exam_note: Parenchyma occurs in both vascular tissues; do not classify the whole vascular tissue as simple.

terms.plain_meaning: फ्लोएम की जीवित संग्रह और स्थानीय आदान-प्रदान करने वाली कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: वितरण मार्ग के पास छोटा भंडारघर।

why_chain.step: Food distribution needs nearby storage and local exchange as well as long-distance flow.
Living phloem parenchyma contributes these associated functions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: phloem parenchyma in many dicot stems.
unpack.consequence: Completes the visible component list and reinforces the mixed-cell nature of complex tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: store and exchange nutrients beside sieve tubes
unpack.level_extra: The visible chart does not establish universal presence in every plant group.

p002-i1.content: Animal Tissues classification tree. Animal Tissues branches to Epithelial Tissue, Muscular Tissue, Connective Tissue and Nervous / Neural Tissue. Epithelial Tissue branches to Simple squamous epithelium, Stratified squamous epithelium, Columnar epithelium, Ciliated columnar epithelium, Cuboidal epithelium and Glandular epithelium. Muscular Tissue branches to Striated muscle, Non-straited muscle [Non-striated muscle] and Cardiac muscle. Connective Tissue branches to Connective tissue proper, Supportive connective tissue and Fluid connective tissue. Connective tissue proper branches to Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue and Fibrous tissue. Supportive connective tissue branches to Cartiage [Cartilage] and Bone. Fluid connective tissue branches to Blood and Lymph. No subdivisions of Nervous / Neural Tissue are shown.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this tree organise?
teacher_understanding.answer: It places four main animal tissue groups below one root and shows further subdivisions of epithelial, muscular and connective tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which branch has three intermediate groups before its examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue divides into connective tissue proper, supportive connective tissue and fluid connective tissue before reaching its named examples.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a student read these arrows?
teacher_understanding.answer: Read downward as 'is divided into', not as a time sequence or a change from one tissue into another.

prerequisites: parent and child branches in a classification
p002-i1.exam_note: Practise matching each leaf to its immediate parent; blood and lymph remain connective tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: जानवरों के शरीर में मिलकर काम करने वाले कोशिका-समूह
terms.everyday_image: शरीर में त्वचा की परत, मांसपेशी और खून

why_chain.step: A body needs covering, movement, support and communication, so its cells perform different specialised jobs.
The tree organises those tissues into four main groups and their shown subdivisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Human body in the lower panel.
unpack.consequence: A liquid tissue can belong to the same broad group as a solid supporting tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: Trace each branch from root to leaf.
unpack.level_extra: Use hierarchy-based matching and odd-one-out questions; branches are not developmental stages.

p002-i2.content: Animal Tissues — root label connecting to the four main tissue groups.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the root of the tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: Animal Tissues is the common heading above the four main branches.

teacher_understanding.question: Which groups descend directly from it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial, muscular, connective and nervous/neural tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does an animal need different tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Covering a surface, producing movement and transmitting signals require cells with different arrangements and abilities.

terms.plain_meaning: मिलकर कोई काम करने वाले कोशिकाओं के समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक काम में जुटी टीम

unpack.example_or_place: Human body.
unpack.consequence: The next branch identifies the tissue's broad job.
unpack.visual_verb: Split into four branches.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse a tissue with a whole organ.

p002-i3.content: Epithelial Tissue — main branch leading to six epithelial types.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this branch contain?
teacher_understanding.answer: It contains the six named epithelial types shown across the bottom of the tree.

teacher_understanding.question: Which kinds of names appear below it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous, stratified squamous, columnar, ciliated columnar, cuboidal and glandular epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is epithelium arranged as a sheet?
teacher_understanding.answer: A continuous sheet can cover or line a surface and regulate contact between that surface and underlying tissues.

p002-i3.exam_note: Separate epithelial examples from connective and muscular examples.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की सतह ढकने या अंगों को अंदर से बिछाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: बिस्तर पर बिछी चादर

unpack.example_or_place: Skin surface and gastrointestinal lining in the lower panel.
unpack.consequence: Shape, number of layers and specialisation distinguish its examples.
unpack.visual_verb: Spread a continuous cell sheet.
unpack.level_extra: Glandular epithelium is also epithelial tissue.

p002-i4.content: Muscular Tissue — branches to Striated muscle, Non-striated muscle and Cardiac muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this main branch show?
teacher_understanding.answer: It groups the three named muscle types together.

teacher_understanding.question: Which muscle types are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Striated, non-striated and cardiac muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: How does muscle produce movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscle cells contract to exert force, moving body parts or contents of organs.

p002-i4.exam_note: Compare skeletal, smooth and cardiac examples in the lower panel.

terms.plain_meaning: सिकुड़कर बल और गति पैदा करने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: कोहनी मोड़ते समय बाजू की मांसपेशी

unpack.example_or_place: Limbs, internal organs and heart.
unpack.consequence: Movement includes internal movements, not just walking.
unpack.visual_verb: Shorten muscle fibres.
unpack.level_extra: Cardiac muscle has striations despite its separate branch here.

p002-i5.content: Connective Tissue — branches to Connective tissue proper, Supportive connective tissue and Fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What is organised below connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Three intermediate groups organise its soft, supportive and fluid examples.

teacher_understanding.question: Which intermediate groups are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue proper, supportive connective tissue and fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can connective tissues look so different?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their material outside the cells, called matrix, can be soft, firm, hard or fluid, supporting different functions.

p002-i5.exam_note: Bone, cartilage, blood and lymph belong to the same broad tissue group.

terms.plain_meaning: जोड़ने, सहारा देने या पदार्थ पहुँचाने में काम आने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: हड्डी का सहारा और खून का बहाव

unpack.example_or_place: Bone, tendon and fat shown below.
unpack.consequence: Do not classify a tissue by hardness alone.
unpack.visual_verb: Branch into soft, supportive and fluid examples.
unpack.level_extra: Matrix explains the apparent contrast between bone and blood.

p002-i6.content: Nervous / Neural Tissue — fourth main branch; no subtypes are shown.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the slash in this label convey?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nervous and neural are alternative names for this main tissue group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower-panel structures relate to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The lower illustration labels brain, spinal cord, nerve, nerve tissue and nerve cell.

teacher_understanding.question: How does nervous tissue coordinate the body?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its specialised cells receive and transmit signals, linking detection of a change with a response.

p002-i6.exam_note: Nervous and neural are not separate main tissue groups.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर में संदेश लेने और पहुँचाने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: गरम बर्तन छूते ही हाथ हटाने का संदेश

unpack.example_or_place: Brain, spinal cord and nerves.
unpack.consequence: Connect the tissue name to the neuron picture below.
unpack.visual_verb: Pass a signal along a branching cell.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish a nerve from a single nerve cell.

p002-i7.content: Striated muscle — child of Muscular Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does striated describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes visible alternating bands in muscle fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent contains this leaf?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscular Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are the bands visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: The contractile components repeat in an orderly pattern, producing light and dark bands.

p002-i7.exam_note: Here the branch corresponds to skeletal muscle; cardiac muscle is also striated in appearance.

terms.plain_meaning: धारियों वाला
terms.everyday_image: धारीदार कपड़े की कतारें

unpack.example_or_place: Skeletal muscle pictured below.
unpack.consequence: Appearance and voluntary control are different criteria.
unpack.visual_verb: Reveal repeated bands.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that every striated muscle is voluntary.

p002-i8.content: Non-straited muscle [Non-striated muscle] — child of Muscular Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does non-striated mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: The muscle lacks the visible cross-banding characteristic of striated fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Which branch contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is one of the three muscular tissue leaves.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it contract without visible bands?
teacher_understanding.answer: It still has contractile components, but they are not arranged in the repeating band pattern seen in skeletal muscle.

p002-i8.exam_note: Link non-striated with smooth muscle in the lower illustration.

terms.plain_meaning: साफ धारियाँ न दिखाने वाली मांसपेशी
terms.everyday_image: आँत की दीवार का धीरे सिकुड़ना

unpack.example_or_place: Walls of the intestine and many other hollow organs, as standard examples.
unpack.consequence: No visible stripes does not mean no contraction.
unpack.visual_verb: Contract a spindle-shaped cell.
unpack.level_extra: Smooth muscle is generally involuntary.

p002-i9.content: Cardiac muscle — child of Muscular Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does cardiac refer to?
teacher_understanding.answer: It refers to the heart.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main branch contains cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscular Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is it useful to distinguish cardiac from skeletal muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: Heart muscle contracts involuntarily and rhythmically, whereas skeletal muscle commonly produces voluntary body movement.

p002-i9.exam_note: Cardiac muscle combines striations with involuntary control.
