terms.plain_meaning: दिल की मांसपेशी
terms.everyday_image: लगातार धड़कता दिल

unpack.example_or_place: Heart wall.
unpack.consequence: It is not the same subtype as the skeletal muscle drawn below.
unpack.visual_verb: Pulse a branching muscle network.
unpack.level_extra: Separate location, appearance and control in statement questions.

p002-i10.content: Connective tissue proper — child of Connective Tissue; parent of Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue and Fibrous tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What role does this label play in the tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is an intermediate group between connective tissue and three named examples.

teacher_understanding.question: Which examples belong here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Areolar, adipose and fibrous tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these examples relate functionally?
teacher_understanding.answer: They contribute to packing, storage and binding rather than forming the rigid skeletal framework or circulating as fluid.

p002-i10.exam_note: Keep its three leaves separate from supportive and fluid connective tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: इस चार्ट में भराव, चर्बी और रेशेदार ऊतकों का समूह
terms.everyday_image: सामान को थामने वाला भराव और बाँधने वाली डोरी

unpack.example_or_place: Soft tissues between and around organs.
unpack.consequence: Adipose is a connective tissue, not a muscle subtype.
unpack.visual_verb: Group three leaves under one branch.
unpack.level_extra: Use the classification scheme printed here.

p002-i11.content: Supportive connective tissue — child of Connective Tissue; parent of Cartilage and Bone.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this branch group?
teacher_understanding.answer: It groups cartilage and bone as supportive connective tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which leaves descend from it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cartilage and Bone.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are they supportive?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their firm extracellular material resists deformation and helps maintain body shape, although cartilage is more flexible than bone.

p002-i11.exam_note: Bone and cartilage are the paired supportive examples.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर को ढाँचा और सहारा देने वाला संयोजी ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: मकान का ढाँचा

unpack.example_or_place: Skeleton and cartilage at joints.
unpack.consequence: Support can be rigid or somewhat flexible.
unpack.visual_verb: Support a body outline.
unpack.level_extra: Do not place tendon under this branch in this particular tree.

p002-i12.content: Fluid connective tissue — child of Connective Tissue; parent of Blood and Lymph.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this branch establish?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood and lymph are included within connective tissue despite their fluid nature.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two examples are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood and Lymph.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a fluid form useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fluid can circulate and transport materials between body regions rather than staying as a fixed supporting sheet.

p002-i12.exam_note: Common classification trap: connective tissue need not be solid.

terms.plain_meaning: तरल रूप वाला संयोजी ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: नलियों में बहता खून

unpack.example_or_place: Blood and lymph circulation.
unpack.consequence: Consistency alone cannot identify a main tissue class.
unpack.visual_verb: Flow along two branches.
unpack.level_extra: Remember the blood–lymph pair.

p002-i13.where_on_page: tree, first connective tissue proper leaf
p002-i13.content: Areolar tissue — child of Connective tissue proper.

teacher_understanding.question: What kind of tissue is areolar tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a loose connective tissue that helps fill spaces and support nearby structures.

teacher_understanding.question: Which immediate group contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue proper.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its loose arrangement help?
teacher_understanding.answer: A flexible network can hold structures together while allowing room for small vessels and movement of tissue fluid.

p002-i13.exam_note: Recognise areolar as connective tissue proper.

terms.plain_meaning: खाली जगह भरने और सहारा देने वाला ढीला संयोजी ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: नाजुक सामान के बीच नरम पैकिंग

unpack.example_or_place: Beneath the skin and around structures, as standard examples.
unpack.consequence: Packing tissue differs from stored fat and dense fibrous tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: Fill spaces with a loose network.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish areolar from adipose by role.

p002-i14.where_on_page: tree, middle connective tissue proper leaf
p002-i14.content: Adipose tissue — child of Connective tissue proper.

teacher_understanding.question: What is adipose tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is connective tissue specialised in storing fat.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue proper.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the body store fat in tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stored fat provides an energy reserve and also contributes to insulation and cushioning.

p002-i14.exam_note: Connect adipose tissue to the fat-cell inset below.

terms.plain_meaning: चर्बी जमा करने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: त्वचा के नीचे नरम चर्बी

unpack.example_or_place: Under skin and around some organs.
unpack.consequence: Fat storage is a connective-tissue function.
unpack.visual_verb: Fill cells with fat.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse tissue type with a nutrient category.

p002-i15.where_on_page: tree, right connective tissue proper leaf
p002-i15.content: Fibrous tissue — child of Connective tissue proper.

teacher_understanding.question: What does fibrous emphasise?
teacher_understanding.answer: It emphasises abundant strong fibres in the tissue's extracellular material.

teacher_understanding.question: Which group contains this leaf?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue proper.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibres help a tissue bind structures?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bundles of fibres resist pulling forces, allowing the tissue to transmit tension without readily separating.

p002-i15.exam_note: Relate fibrous connective tissue to the tendon example.

terms.plain_meaning: मजबूत रेशों से भरपूर ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: कई धागों से बनी मजबूत रस्सी

unpack.example_or_place: Tendons, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Binding strength is different from muscle contraction.
unpack.visual_verb: Bundle fibres and pull.
unpack.level_extra: Tendon is connective, not muscular tissue.

p002-i16.content: Cartiage [Cartilage] — child of Supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What is cartilage?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a firm but relatively flexible supporting connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue is paired with cartilage here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone, under supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cartilage useful where some flexibility is needed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its matrix can support shape while allowing more bending than hard mineralised bone.

p002-i16.exam_note: Pair cartilage with bone without treating them as identical.

terms.plain_meaning: मजबूत पर कुछ लचीला सहारा देने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: बाहरी कान को हल्का मोड़ना

unpack.example_or_place: External ear and joint surfaces, as standard examples.
unpack.consequence: Supporting tissue need not be as hard as bone.
unpack.visual_verb: Bend a firm support gently.
unpack.level_extra: Cartilage is not muscle.

p002-i17.content: Bone — child of Supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What is bone in this classification?
teacher_understanding.answer: A supportive connective tissue, rather than a separate fifth main tissue class.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main group ultimately contains bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is bone hard?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mineral salts deposited in its matrix provide rigidity, while its organic components contribute toughness.

p002-i17.exam_note: Trace Bone → Supportive connective tissue → Connective Tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर को कठोर सहारा देने वाला जीवित ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: बाजू की हड्डी

unpack.example_or_place: Human skeleton.
unpack.consequence: A hard tissue can still be living and cellular.
unpack.visual_verb: Hold the body upright.
unpack.level_extra: Bone is a tissue; a whole bone also contains other tissues.

p002-i18.content: Blood — child of Fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the tree say about blood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It places blood within fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue shares blood's immediate parent?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lymph.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can blood count as a connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells are carried in a fluid extracellular matrix, plasma, and it links body regions by transporting materials.

p002-i18.exam_note: Blood is not epithelial tissue merely because it travels inside vessels.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर में पदार्थ ले जाने वाला बहता ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: चोट लगने पर दिखने वाला खून

unpack.example_or_place: Heart and blood vessels.
unpack.consequence: Fluidity does not exclude a tissue from connective tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: Carry cells through liquid.
unpack.level_extra: Plasma is the fluid matrix, not the entire blood.

p002-i19.content: Lymph — child of Fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What kind of tissue is lymph in this tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fluid connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other named fluid connective tissue appears beside it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood.

teacher_understanding.question: How is lymph linked to fluid around cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Some tissue fluid enters lymphatic vessels and is then called lymph; this pathway helps return excess fluid to the bloodstream.

p002-i19.exam_note: Remember both members of the fluid connective pair.

terms.plain_meaning: लसीका नलियों में बहने वाला ऊतक-द्रव
terms.everyday_image: गलियों से पानी जुटाकर मुख्य रास्ते तक लौटाने वाली नालियाँ

unpack.example_or_place: Lymphatic vessels.
unpack.consequence: The body's transport tissues are not limited to blood.
unpack.visual_verb: Collect tissue fluid into vessels.
unpack.level_extra: Lymph is not a nerve fluid or a muscle subtype.

p002-i20.content: Simple squamous epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the name describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single layer of thin, flattened epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main group contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a thin single layer useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: It offers a short distance for diffusion, which helps exchange across surfaces such as lung air sacs.

p002-i20.exam_note: Simple describes layer number; squamous describes cell shape.

terms.plain_meaning: चपटी कोशिकाओं की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: फर्श पर टाइलों की एक पतली तह

unpack.example_or_place: Lung alveoli, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Contrast thin exchange surfaces with multilayer protection.
unpack.visual_verb: Flatten cells into one sheet.
unpack.level_extra: Do not equate simple with unimportant.

p002-i21.content: Stratified squamous epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does stratified squamous mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: There are several cell layers, with flattened cells at the exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Which nearby leaf provides the direct layer-number contrast?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are several layers useful at exposed surfaces?
teacher_understanding.answer: Surface cells may be rubbed away while deeper layers continue protecting underlying tissue.

p002-i21.exam_note: The surface-cell shape names the stratified epithelium.

terms.plain_meaning: कई परतों वाला ऊतक जिसकी ऊपर की कोशिकाएँ चपटी हैं
terms.everyday_image: सुरक्षा के लिए कपड़े की कई तहें

unpack.example_or_place: Skin epidermis, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: More layers favour protection rather than a short diffusion path.
unpack.visual_verb: Stack layers under flattened surface cells.
unpack.level_extra: Not every cell in every layer has to be flat.

p002-i22.content: Columnar epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What shape does columnar indicate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells taller than they are wide, like columns.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower-panel picture gives a more specific columnar label?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple columnar.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this cell form relate to function?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tall cells can contain machinery for absorption and secretion, common activities in digestive linings.

p002-i22.exam_note: Columnar is a shape term; it does not itself mean ciliated.

terms.plain_meaning: खंभे जैसी लंबी कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: कतार में खड़े खंभे

unpack.example_or_place: Intestinal lining, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Cilia are a separate surface specialisation.
unpack.visual_verb: Raise cells into pillars.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish columnar from cuboidal by proportions.

p002-i23.content: Ciliated columnar epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What extra feature does ciliated add?
teacher_understanding.answer: Hair-like projections called cilia occur on the exposed surface of columnar cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower picture corresponds to this leaf?
teacher_understanding.answer: The epithelial inset labels a ciliated columnar example with projections on its upper surface.

teacher_understanding.question: How do cilia help a lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: Coordinated beating moves material along the surface, such as mucus in respiratory passages.

p002-i23.exam_note: Cilia move material; do not confuse them with absorptive microvilli.

terms.plain_meaning: ऊपर चलने वाले महीन रोम लिए खंभेनुमा कोशिकाओं की परत
terms.everyday_image: एक दिशा में साथ चलती छोटी झाड़ुएँ

unpack.example_or_place: Respiratory passages and oviducts, as standard examples.
unpack.consequence: Surface movement distinguishes it from non-ciliated columnar epithelium.
unpack.visual_verb: Sweep particles along a surface.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid assuming all columnar epithelium has cilia.

p002-i24.content: Cuboidal epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What does cuboidal describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells whose height and width are approximately similar, giving a cube-like appearance.

teacher_understanding.question: Which lower-panel label corresponds to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple cuboidal.

teacher_understanding.question: How can cuboidal cells serve a tubular lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: They form a compact lining that can absorb or secrete substances, as in many kidney tubules.

p002-i24.exam_note: Associate cube-like cells with cuboidal, not columnar.

terms.plain_meaning: लगभग घन जैसी कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: खेल का पासा

unpack.example_or_place: Kidney tubules, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Cell proportions distinguish it from squamous and columnar forms.
unpack.visual_verb: Arrange cubes into a lining.
unpack.level_extra: The lower illustration specifies one layer with 'simple'.

p002-i25.content: Glandular epithelium — child of Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What is glandular epithelium specialised for?
teacher_understanding.answer: Producing and releasing substances, or secretion.

teacher_understanding.question: Which main tissue group contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are gland cells useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: The body needs substances such as sweat, mucus and digestive secretions delivered to particular sites.

p002-i25.exam_note: Glandular describes specialisation, unlike shape terms such as cuboidal.

terms.plain_meaning: पदार्थ बनाकर छोड़ने में विशेषीकृत उपकला
terms.everyday_image: पसीना बनाने वाली ग्रंथि

unpack.example_or_place: Sweat and salivary glands, as standard examples.
unpack.consequence: Epithelium does more than act as a passive cover.
unpack.visual_verb: Release droplets from cells.
unpack.level_extra: It is not a fifth primary animal tissue group.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this panel add to the classification tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies tissue appearances and body-location links for the four main tissue groups.

teacher_understanding.question: Which four insets surround the body?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscular tissue, nerve tissue, epithelial tissue and connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the body pointers be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They link representative tissues to body regions; they do not mean that a whole organ consists of only one tissue.

p002-i26.exam_note: Useful for image recognition and tissue–location matching.

terms.plain_meaning: किसी खोखले अंग के अंदर बिछी परत
terms.everyday_image: नली की भीतरी सतह

why_chain.step: An organ must combine covering, movement, support and communication.
The panel links the four tissue groups to representative body sites and appearances.

unpack.example_or_place: Human skin, digestive tract, heart, skeleton and nervous system.
unpack.consequence: Classify a pictured tissue before matching its location or function.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom from body region into tissue cells.
unpack.level_extra: Do not mistake a representative pointer for an exclusive distribution.

p002-i27.content: Muscular tissue — labels the inset showing three muscle-cell appearances.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this inset display?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cardiac, skeletal and smooth muscle drawings under muscular tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which names differ from the upper tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: The lower panel uses Skeletal muscle and Smooth muscle where the upper muscle branch uses Striated muscle and Non-striated muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: How are these naming systems connected?
teacher_understanding.answer: The skeletal example is striated and the smooth example is non-striated; cardiac muscle also has striations but is separately named for its heart location.

p002-i27.exam_note: Reconcile names rather than memorising the panels as unrelated lists.

terms.plain_meaning: सिकुड़कर बल पैदा करने वाले ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: बाजू मोड़ना और दिल धड़कना

unpack.example_or_place: Three muscle sketches at upper left of body.
unpack.consequence: Location names and appearance names can refer to related examples.
unpack.visual_verb: Match the two sets of labels.
unpack.level_extra: Keep the cardiac striation exception explicit.

p002-i28.content: Muscle cells — arrows associate the common label with the three muscle drawings.

teacher_understanding.question: What common unit is being illustrated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscle cells, shown with different shapes in the three muscle examples.

teacher_understanding.question: Which examples share this label?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cardiac, skeletal and smooth muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: How can differently shaped cells still be muscular?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their shared capacity is contraction, even though their arrangements and control differ.

p002-i28.exam_note: Relate cell appearance to tissue identity.

terms.plain_meaning: मांसपेशी बनाने वाली सिकुड़ने योग्य कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: बल लगाते समय छोटी होती मांसपेशी

unpack.example_or_place: The three red muscle drawings.
unpack.consequence: Shared function does not imply identical shape.
unpack.visual_verb: Compare branching, cylindrical and spindle forms.
unpack.level_extra: A muscle fibre is a muscle cell, not merely a non-living thread.

p002-i29.content: Cardiac muscle — labels the branching red muscle drawing connected toward the heart region.

teacher_understanding.question: What appearance is used for cardiac muscle?
teacher_understanding.answer: A branching red muscle network.

teacher_understanding.question: Which body region is linked to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heart region of the central body drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is coordinated contraction important there?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heart must generate organised pumping contractions to move blood effectively.

p002-i29.exam_note: Branching appearance, heart location and involuntary action are useful distinguishing features.

terms.plain_meaning: दिल की दीवार की मांसपेशी
terms.everyday_image: छाती में महसूस होती धड़कन

unpack.example_or_place: Heart.
unpack.consequence: Branching muscle is not a branching nerve cell.
unpack.visual_verb: Contract connected branches rhythmically.
unpack.level_extra: Cardiac muscle is striated but involuntary.

p002-i30.content: Skeletal muscle — labels a bundle of long cylindrical red fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: What form does the skeletal muscle picture show?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long cylindrical fibres grouped in a bundle.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree label corresponds to this example?
teacher_understanding.answer: The striated-muscle branch represents the skeletal example in this introductory scheme.

teacher_understanding.question: How does skeletal muscle move a limb?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its contraction pulls through tendons on bones across joints.

p002-i30.exam_note: Skeletal muscle produces movement; tendon transmits its pull.

terms.plain_meaning: हड्डियों को खींचकर शरीर चलाने वाली मांसपेशी
terms.everyday_image: बाजू की मांसपेशी से कोहनी मोड़ना

unpack.example_or_place: Limb muscles.
unpack.consequence: Link muscular and connective tissue through the tendon example.
unpack.visual_verb: Pull a bone with a shortening bundle.
unpack.level_extra: Usually under voluntary control.

p002-i31.content: Smooth muscle — labels elongated spindle-shaped red cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What cell shape is shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: The smooth muscle cells are elongated and taper at their ends.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper-tree term describes this muscle's appearance?
teacher_understanding.answer: Non-striated muscle.

teacher_understanding.question: How does smooth muscle help digestion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Contractions in the gut wall move and mix its contents without needing conscious instructions for each contraction.

p002-i31.exam_note: Spindle-shaped, non-striated and generally involuntary are linked features.

terms.plain_meaning: बिना साफ धारियों वाली, दोनों सिरों पर पतली मांसपेशी कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: दोनों सिरों से पतला बेलन

unpack.example_or_place: Digestive tract walls, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Internal movement does not require skeletal muscle.
unpack.visual_verb: Narrow a tube by contraction.
unpack.level_extra: Smooth does not mean inactive.

p002-i32.content: Brain — leader line points to the brain in the head.

teacher_understanding.question: What structure is identified in the head?
teacher_understanding.answer: The brain.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue group is associated with the brain?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nervous tissue is a principal functional tissue of the brain.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the brain contribute to coordination?
teacher_understanding.answer: Networks of nerve cells process information and organise responses.

p002-i32.exam_note: Link brain and spinal cord with nervous tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: सिर के भीतर संदेश समझने और कार्यों का समन्वय करने वाला अंग
terms.everyday_image: शरीर का नियंत्रण कक्ष

unpack.example_or_place: Inside the skull.
unpack.consequence: A tissue class is illustrated through a familiar organ.
unpack.visual_verb: Highlight the brain in the head.
unpack.level_extra: The brain is an organ, not a single neuron.

p002-i33.content: Spinal cord — leader line points toward the nervous structure descending from the brain through the neck.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cord-like nervous structure descending from the brain.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue system does it illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nervous tissue context of the body illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the spinal cord connect the body and brain?
teacher_understanding.answer: It carries nerve signals between them and also participates in many reflex pathways.

p002-i33.exam_note: Do not confuse spinal cord with the bony vertebral column.

terms.plain_meaning: रीढ़ की हड्डियों के भीतर सुरक्षित संदेश ले जाने वाला तंत्रिका भाग
terms.everyday_image: सुरक्षा-कवर में रखी मुख्य तार

unpack.example_or_place: Within the vertebral canal.
unpack.consequence: The surrounding bone and the cord belong to different tissue contexts.
unpack.visual_verb: Trace downward from the brain.
unpack.level_extra: Spinal cord is nervous tissue; vertebrae provide skeletal protection.

p002-i34.content: Nerve — leader line points to a yellow nerve pathway near the shoulder and upper arm.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this body pointer identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A nerve pathway near the shoulder and upper arm.

teacher_understanding.question: Which nearby inset relates to this pathway?
teacher_understanding.answer: The Nerve tissue inset.

teacher_understanding.question: How is a nerve different from one nerve cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: A nerve contains bundles of nerve fibres with supporting coverings; it is not one complete neuron.

p002-i34.exam_note: Distinguish nerve, neuron and muscle fibre.

terms.plain_meaning: संदेश ले जाने वाले तंत्रिका-रेशों का बंडल
terms.everyday_image: कई तारों वाली केबल

unpack.example_or_place: Pathways running into the limbs.
unpack.consequence: A single cell picture represents a unit of nervous tissue, not an entire nerve.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom from cable to individual fibres.
unpack.level_extra: A nerve carries signals rather than actively pulling bones.

p002-i35.content: Nerve tissue — labels the inset containing branching nerve-cell drawings.

teacher_understanding.question: What appearance is emphasised in the inset?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells with several branching projections.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper-tree branch matches this inset?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nervous / Neural Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are projections useful in this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: They provide routes for receiving information and passing signals between cells and body regions.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर के संदेशों को ग्रहण और आगे पहुँचाने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: एक-दूसरे से जुड़ा संदेश-जाल

unpack.example_or_place: Brain, spinal cord and nerves.
unpack.consequence: Branching is linked to communication, unlike muscle contraction.
unpack.visual_verb: Connect branching cells with signals.
unpack.level_extra: Nervous tissue also includes supporting cells, although this inset emphasises neurons.

p002-i36.content: Nerve cell — leader line identifies one of the illustrated branching cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the standard name for a nerve cell?
teacher_understanding.answer: A neuron.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature helps identify it here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its branching projections extending from the cell body.

teacher_understanding.question: How do its extensions help communication?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dendrites mainly receive inputs, while an axon carries signals toward other cells.

p002-i36.exam_note: Neuron is a cell; nerve is a bundle of fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: संदेश लेने और पहुँचाने वाली विशेष कोशिका; neuron

unpack.example_or_place: Branching cells in the nerve inset.
unpack.consequence: Separate the cell level from the tissue and organ levels.
unpack.visual_verb: Receive a signal and send it onward.
unpack.level_extra: Axon and dendrites are explanatory additions, not printed labels here.

p002-i37.content: Epithelial tissue — labels the inset of cell sheets and a layered skin-surface example.

teacher_understanding.question: What common arrangement do these examples show?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells arranged as continuous sheets, including a thicker layered example.

teacher_understanding.question: Which four shape examples are explicitly named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Ciliated columnar, simple columnar, simple cuboidal and simple squamous.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can epithelial sheets have different thicknesses?
teacher_understanding.answer: Thin sheets favour exchange, while multiple layers provide more resistance to abrasion.

p002-i37.exam_note: Use shape and layer count together when identifying epithelium.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास जुड़ी कोशिकाओं से बनी ढकने या अंदर बिछने वाली परत

unpack.example_or_place: Gut lining and skin surface in this inset.
unpack.consequence: One broad tissue group can serve exchange, secretion and protection.
unpack.visual_verb: Compare thin sheets with stacked layers.
unpack.level_extra: The tree names more epithelial types than this inset individually illustrates.

p002-i38.content: Lining of gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs — broad location label associated with the epithelial inset and connected to the abdominal region.

teacher_understanding.question: What does a lining mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The layer facing the inner space of a hollow organ, rather than the organ's whole wall.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations does the printed label name?
teacher_understanding.answer: The gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a hollow organ need a specialised lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its inner surface contacts contents and may need protection, absorption or secretion depending on the site.

p002-i38.exam_note: Do not infer that all pictured epithelial forms occur throughout the gastrointestinal tract.

terms.plain_meaning: भोजन के पाचन और आगे जाने का पेट-आँत वाला मार्ग
terms.everyday_image: शरीर के भीतर भोजन की गुजरने वाली नली

terms.plain_meaning: जिन अंगों के भीतर खाली जगह होती है
terms.everyday_image: मूत्राशय जैसी थैली

why_chain.step: Food and fluids contact the inner surface of digestive organs.
A specialised epithelial lining protects or exchanges substances according to the location.

unpack.example_or_place: Digestive tract in the abdomen.
unpack.consequence: The epithelial lining and muscular wall have different roles.
unpack.visual_verb: Cut open a tube and highlight its inner sheet.
unpack.level_extra: Location-specific epithelial types vary along the digestive tract.

p002-i39.where_on_page: epithelial inset, first small tissue drawing
p002-i39.content: Ciliated columnar — identifies tall epithelial cells bearing numerous fine projections on their upper surface.

teacher_understanding.question: What surface feature is drawn?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fine projections above the tall cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree leaf matches this picture?
teacher_understanding.answer: Ciliated columnar epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the projection layer work?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cilia beat together to move material along the surface rather than moving the entire epithelial sheet.

p002-i39.exam_note: Recognise tall cells plus surface cilia.

terms.plain_meaning: ऊपर महीन चलायमान रोम वाली लंबी कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: खंभों की कतार पर लगी छोटी झाड़ुएँ

unpack.example_or_place: Respiratory lining, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: The surface specialisation supplies a movement function.
unpack.visual_verb: Beat cilia in waves.
unpack.level_extra: This is not evidence that the entire intestinal lining is ciliated.

p002-i40.where_on_page: epithelial inset, second small tissue drawing
p002-i40.content: Simple columnar — identifies a single layer of tall epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What two properties does this name specify?
teacher_understanding.answer: One cell layer and a tall, column-like cell shape.

teacher_understanding.question: Which adjoining picture adds a separate surface feature?
teacher_understanding.answer: The ciliated columnar picture to its left.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is one layer helpful for absorption?
teacher_understanding.answer: Absorbed substances cross a relatively short epithelial path before reaching underlying tissues.

p002-i40.exam_note: Distinguish simple columnar from both cuboidal and ciliated columnar.

terms.plain_meaning: खंभेनुमा कोशिकाओं की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: एक कतार में खड़े लंबे खंभे

unpack.example_or_place: Intestinal lining, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: One-layer arrangement and shape are independent descriptors.
unpack.visual_verb: Show a single row of tall cells.
unpack.level_extra: Simple refers to layers, not absence of specialised function.

p002-i41.where_on_page: epithelial inset, third small tissue drawing
p002-i41.content: Simple cubodial [Simple cuboidal] — identifies a single sheet of cube-like epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this picture's label specify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single cell layer with approximately cube-like cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree label is the broader matching name?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cuboidal epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ visually from simple columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells are about as tall as wide, rather than distinctly taller than wide.

p002-i41.exam_note: Match cuboidal with kidney-tubule examples at standard textbook level.

terms.plain_meaning: घन जैसी कोशिकाओं की एक परत
terms.everyday_image: पासों की एक कतार

unpack.example_or_place: Many kidney tubules.
unpack.consequence: Cell height separates this from the tall-cell picture beside it.
unpack.visual_verb: Compare cell height and width.
unpack.level_extra: The printed 'simple' adds layer count to the tree's shape label.

p002-i42.where_on_page: epithelial inset, fourth small tissue drawing
p002-i42.content: Simple squamous — identifies a thin sheet of flattened epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes this example visually distinctive?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is shown as a much thinner, flatter cell sheet than the columnar and cuboidal examples.

teacher_understanding.question: Which upper-tree label matches it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does thinness suit exchange?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thinner barrier reduces the distance across which substances must diffuse.

p002-i42.exam_note: Do not confuse this thin sheet with the layered skin example below.

terms.plain_meaning: चपटी कोशिकाओं की एक पतली तह
terms.everyday_image: एक तह में बिछी पतली टाइलें

unpack.example_or_place: Lung air sacs, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Thin exchange epithelium contrasts with thick protective epithelium.
unpack.visual_verb: Pass particles across a thin sheet.
unpack.level_extra: Squamous describes flattened shape, not the presence of scales on skin.

p002-i43.where_on_page: epithelial inset, bottom-left label beside thick block
p002-i43.content: Skin surface — identifies the multilayer epithelial example below the four smaller drawings.

teacher_understanding.question: What visible arrangement is associated with skin surface?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thicker block composed of several cell layers.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree type corresponds to the protective epidermal arrangement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stratified squamous epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are multiple layers useful on skin?
teacher_understanding.answer: The surface experiences friction and cell loss, so deeper layers help maintain a protective barrier.

p002-i43.exam_note: The epidermis is epithelial; whole skin also contains other tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर को बाहर से ढकने वाली त्वचा की ऊपरी सतह
terms.everyday_image: हथेली पर बार-बार होने वाली रगड़

why_chain.step: Exposed body surfaces face rubbing and wear.
Several epithelial layers help protect underlying tissue despite surface cell loss.

unpack.example_or_place: Outer epidermal surface.
unpack.consequence: Protection explains the contrast with a single thin exchange layer.
unpack.visual_verb: Rub away surface cells while deeper layers remain.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the statement that all of skin is epithelium.

p002-i44.content: Basement membrane — bent leader line points to the underside of the layered epithelial block.

teacher_understanding.question: What position does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The supporting boundary beneath the epithelial block.

teacher_understanding.question: Which side of epithelium is associated with it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The basal side, facing underlying tissue rather than the exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the basement membrane help epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides an extracellular supporting sheet that helps anchor epithelial cells to underlying tissue.

p002-i44.exam_note: Basement membrane is not another full layer of epithelial cells.

terms.plain_meaning: उपकला के नीचे की पतली सहायक आधार-परत
terms.everyday_image: टाइलों को टिकाने वाली नीचे की आधार-परत

why_chain.step: A cell sheet needs attachment to the tissue underneath.
A supporting basement membrane helps anchor and organise that sheet.

unpack.example_or_place: Under the illustrated skin epithelium.
unpack.consequence: Distinguish exposed surface from attached basal surface.
unpack.visual_verb: Underline the base of the cell block.
unpack.level_extra: Do not mistake it for the cell's plasma membrane.

p002-i45.content: Connective tissue — labels the inset containing Tendon, Bone and Fat cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this inset illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Three contrasting connective examples: tendon, bone and fat cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which example corresponds to supportive connective tissue in the tree?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do these examples have different appearances?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dense fibres suit tension in tendons, mineralised matrix suits support in bone, and fat-filled cells suit storage and cushioning.

p002-i45.exam_note: The inset is representative, not the full connective-tissue list.

terms.plain_meaning: जोड़ने, सहारा देने और भराव जैसे काम करने वाले ऊतकों का समूह

unpack.example_or_place: Tendons, bones and body fat.
unpack.consequence: A single broad category contains different physical forms.

p002-i46.content: Tendon — identifies the yellow bundle of parallel fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: What form is used to depict a tendon?
teacher_understanding.answer: A compact bundle of parallel fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Which structures does a tendon typically connect?
teacher_understanding.answer: Muscle to bone.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the fibrous arrangement serve movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Strong fibre bundles transmit a contracting muscle's pull to bone.

p002-i46.exam_note: Tendon connects muscle to bone; ligament generally connects bone to bone.

terms.plain_meaning: मांसपेशी का खिंचाव हड्डी तक पहुँचाने वाली मजबूत रेशेदार पट्टी
terms.everyday_image: एड़ी के पीछे महसूस होने वाली कड़ी डोरी

why_chain.step: A shortening muscle needs to transfer its pull to the skeleton.
A strong tendon links it to bone and transmits the force.

unpack.example_or_place: Achilles tendon behind the ankle, as a standard example.
unpack.consequence: Tendon supports movement without itself being muscle.
unpack.visual_verb: Transmit a pull through parallel fibres.
unpack.level_extra: Tendon–ligament distinction is a useful matching-question trap.

p002-i47.content: Bone — identifies the pale long-bone drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What is shown as the bone example?
teacher_understanding.answer: A pale elongated bone with widened ends.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tree subgroup contains bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Supportive connective tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How can bone contribute to movement as well as support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bones act as levers when muscles pull on them across joints.

p002-i47.exam_note: Recognise bone as connective tissue despite its rigid appearance.

terms.plain_meaning: कठोर ढाँचा देने वाला जीवित ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: चलते समय भार संभालती पैर की हड्डी

unpack.example_or_place: Long bones of the limbs.
unpack.consequence: Bone and tendon cooperate with muscle but have different roles.
unpack.visual_verb: Rotate a bone at a joint.
unpack.level_extra: A bone drawing represents the tissue example schematically.

p002-i48.content: Fat and other Soft padding tissue — label associated with soft cushioning tissue and the fat-cell example.

teacher_understanding.question: What role is highlighted by this printed phrase?
teacher_understanding.answer: Soft padding associated with fat and other soft tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which formal tree leaf corresponds to fat tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is soft padding useful around body structures?
teacher_understanding.answer: Compressible tissue can cushion pressure and help protect structures from mechanical shocks.

p002-i48.exam_note: Treat padding as a function, not as a separately named main tissue class.

terms.plain_meaning: दबाव और झटके कम करने वाला नरम भराव ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: नाजुक वस्तु के चारों ओर रखी नरम गद्दी

why_chain.step: Body structures face pressure and occasional mechanical shocks.
Soft fat-containing tissue helps cushion them.

unpack.example_or_place: Fat around organs and beneath skin, as standard examples.
unpack.consequence: Connect the familiar cushioning role with adipose tissue in the tree.
unpack.visual_verb: Compress a soft pad around a structure.
unpack.level_extra: Adipose also stores energy; padding is not its sole function.

p002-i49.content: Fat cells — arrow points to a cluster of rounded yellow-orange cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What cell appearance is shown here?
teacher_understanding.answer: A cluster of rounded yellow-orange cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue do fat cells characterise?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fat cells serve as an energy reserve?
teacher_understanding.answer: They store lipid that can be mobilised when the body needs energy.

p002-i49.exam_note: Link fat cells → adipose tissue → connective tissue proper.

terms.plain_meaning: चर्बी जमा करने वाली कोशिकाएँ
terms.everyday_image: बाद में उपयोग के लिए भंडार भरना

unpack.example_or_place: Adipose tissue beneath skin and around organs.
unpack.consequence: A cell-level drawing connects with a named tissue-level branch.
unpack.visual_verb: Fill and empty stored fat in rounded cells.
unpack.level_extra: The drawing is schematic, not a literal colour guide for microscopy.

p003-i1.content:
There are mainly four different types of tissues present in our body.
1. Epithelial- provides covering or lining
2. Muscular- helps in movement
3. Neural- responds to stimuli
4. Connective- supports, links and cushions

teacher_understanding.question: Which four main tissue types does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial, muscular, neural and connective tissue form the four main groups listed here.

teacher_understanding.question: How do their main roles differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Epithelial tissue covers or lines; muscular tissue enables movement; neural tissue responds to stimuli; connective tissue supports, links and cushions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the body need these different kinds rather than one uniform tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Covering a surface, generating force, detecting changes and supporting parts demand different cell arrangements and activities. Division of work allows specialised tissues to perform these jobs effectively.

prerequisites: A tissue as a group of cells performing related functions
p003-i1.exam_note: Core matching and odd-one-out material: distinguish response to stimuli from movement and covering from support.

terms.plain_meaning: ढकने या अंदर की सतह पर अस्तर बनाने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: बिस्तर पर बिछी चादर

terms.plain_meaning: सिकुड़कर गति में मदद करने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: हाथ मोड़ते समय काम करती मांसपेशी

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसे बदलाव जिन पर शरीर प्रतिक्रिया करता है
terms.everyday_image: गर्म बर्तन छूने पर हाथ हटाना

terms.plain_meaning: हिस्सों को जोड़ने, सहारा देने और झटका कम करने वाला ऊतक
terms.everyday_image: नाज़ुक चीज़ के चारों ओर रखी गद्दी

why_chain.step: The body needs surfaces protected, parts moved, changes detected and structures supported.
Different tissues divide these jobs rather than using the same structure for all of them.

unpack.example_or_place: Use the learner's arm: its covering, movement and response to touch illustrate different tissue jobs.
unpack.consequence: The remainder of this page examines the covering-and-lining group.
unpack.visual_verb: Separate four tissue roles around one body outline.
unpack.level_extra: Use function-based statement matching without assuming that a tissue has only one possible function.

p003-i2.content:
Epithelium covers most organs and cavities within the body.
It also forms a barrier to keep different body systems separate.

teacher_understanding.question: What physical role does epithelium play?
teacher_understanding.answer: It forms a covering or lining that also separates body compartments as a barrier.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the page place these epithelial coverings?
teacher_understanding.answer: Over most organs and within body cavities.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a lining more than a passive wrapper?
teacher_understanding.answer: A continuous cellular boundary helps control contact and movement of materials between compartments; different linings can specialise for different exchanges.

p003-i2.exam_note: Covering, lining and separation are defining epithelial roles.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर के भीतर की जगहें
terms.everyday_image: कमरे की अंदरूनी जगह

terms.plain_meaning: दो हिस्सों को अलग रखने वाली रोक
terms.everyday_image: दो कमरों के बीच दीवार

why_chain.step: Body compartments need boundaries so that their contents do not mix freely.
An epithelial covering provides a separating interface.

unpack.example_or_place: The digestive tract lining, listed later in the table, gives a familiar internal-surface example.
unpack.consequence: The next bullets explain the close packing that makes a sheet-like boundary possible.
unpack.visual_verb: Wrap an organ and line an internal space.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish an internal lining from a tissue lying deep beneath that lining.

p003-i3.where_on_page: upper middle, third and fourth bullets
p003-i3.content:
Epithelial tissue cells are tightly packed and form a continuous sheet.
They have only a small amount of cementing material between them and almost no intercellular spaces.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement makes epithelium sheet-like?
teacher_understanding.answer: Closely packed cells, very little material between them and almost no intercellular spaces create a continuous cellular layer.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the small amount of cementing material situated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Between neighbouring epithelial cells rather than as a large space separating them.

teacher_understanding.question: How does close packing support the barrier role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Closely joined neighbouring cells reduce open gaps across a surface, like closely laid tiles. This supports a continuous boundary rather than a loose cellular mesh.

p003-i3.exam_note: A common distinguishing statement is scant intercellular material, not abundant matrix.

terms.plain_meaning: कोशिकाओं के बीच की खाली जगहें
terms.everyday_image: फर्श की टाइलों के बीच के अंतर

terms.plain_meaning: कोशिकाओं के बीच उन्हें साथ रखने में मदद करने वाला पदार्थ
terms.everyday_image: टाइलों के बीच थोड़ा सा जोड़ने वाला मसाला

why_chain.step: A boundary with many open gaps would not make an effective continuous covering.
Epithelial cells lie tightly together with little intervening material.

unpack.example_or_place: Visualise the mouth lining as closely arranged cells rather than widely scattered dots.
unpack.consequence: Cell arrangement explains how epithelium can cover and separate surfaces.
unpack.visual_verb: Close gaps between neighbouring cells.
unpack.level_extra: Do not turn 'almost no spaces' into the claim that no material can cross epithelium.

p003-i4.content: All epithelium is usually separated from the underlying tissue by an extracellular fibrous basement membrane.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the basement membrane described here?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is an extracellular fibrous layer separating epithelium from the tissue underneath.

teacher_understanding.question: Where should it be placed in a diagram?
teacher_understanding.answer: At the interface below the epithelial sheet and above the underlying tissue, not between every pair of epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does an epithelial sheet need a supporting interface?
teacher_understanding.answer: A surface sheet needs anchorage to the tissue below. The basement membrane provides support and attachment at that interface.

p003-i4.exam_note: Know the location and extracellular nature; do not confuse basement membrane with cell membrane.

terms.plain_meaning: कोशिका के बाहर स्थित
terms.everyday_image: घर के बाहर का रास्ता, घर का अंदरूनी कमरा नहीं

terms.plain_meaning: एपिथीलियम के नीचे की सहायक परत
terms.everyday_image: टाइलों के नीचे बिछा आधार

why_chain.step: A surface sheet needs attachment to the tissue beneath it.
The basement membrane provides a supporting interface below the epithelial cells.

unpack.example_or_place: In a tissue cross-section, locate the thin base immediately beneath the epithelial cells.
unpack.consequence: Separate the cellular epithelial sheet from its non-cellular supporting layer.
unpack.visual_verb: Lift the epithelial sheet to reveal its base.
unpack.level_extra: Preserve the book's qualifier 'usually'; avoid converting it into an unsupported absolute.

p003-i5.content: Epithelial cells often acquire additional specialisation as gland cells, which can secrete substances at the epithelial surface. Sometimes a portion of the epithelial tissue folds inward, and a multicellular gland is formed. This is glandular epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: What extra job can epithelial cells acquire?
teacher_understanding.answer: They can specialise as gland cells that release substances at an epithelial surface; this secretory specialisation is glandular epithelium.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page describe formation of a multicellular gland?
teacher_understanding.answer: A portion of the epithelial sheet folds inward, producing a gland made of multiple cells.

teacher_understanding.question: When is this inward-folding route relevant?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes it as something that happens sometimes during gland formation, not as a compulsory change in every epithelial sheet.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is secretion a specialisation rather than simply covering?
teacher_understanding.answer: Secretion requires cells to produce or handle material and release it, adding an active chemical job to the physical job of making a surface.

p003-i5.exam_note: Link glandular epithelium to secretion and inward folding; distinguish absorption from secretion.

terms.plain_meaning: पदार्थ बनाकर या तैयार करके बाहर छोड़ना
terms.everyday_image: लार ग्रंथि से लार निकलना

terms.plain_meaning: कई कोशिकाओं से बनी स्राव करने वाली ग्रंथि
terms.everyday_image: कई काम करने वालों की एक छोटी उत्पादन इकाई

why_chain.step: Body surfaces may need useful substances delivered onto them.
Epithelial cells specialise for secretion, and an inward fold can form a multicellular gland.

unpack.example_or_place: Salivary glands provide a familiar secretion example; their ducts appear in the table.
unpack.consequence: Epithelium is not merely a passive covering; it can form secretory structures.
unpack.visual_verb: Fold a sheet inward and release droplets.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid treating 'sometimes' as 'all glands arise by this exact visible arrangement'.

p003-i6.where_on_page: upper right, four vertically stacked tissue drawings
p003-i6.content: Four separate epithelial tissue drawings show (a) a thin sheet of flat cells, (b) many stacked layers with flattened surface cells, (c) a single layer of cube-like cells, and (d) tall cells with cilia at their exposed surface. Each drawing rests on a contrasting basal strip. These are separate examples, not stages connected by arrows.
p003-i6.type_note: The image contains a teachable tissue figure, not non-teachable material.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the figure make visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: It contrasts flat, multilayered, cube-like and tall ciliated epithelial arrangements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visual criteria distinguish the examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Layer number distinguishes the stratified example, while cell shape and surface cilia distinguish the other drawings.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a learner identify these drawings rather than memorise their positions?
teacher_understanding.answer: First count layers, then inspect the surface cell shape, and finally look for projections such as cilia. This produces a reusable recognition method.

p003-i6.exam_note: Useful for diagram identification and matching appearance with tissue names.

Count layers and compare cell shapes to recognise the illustrated types.

p003-i7.content: (a) Squamous — points to the thin sheet of flattened, irregularly outlined cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What appearance does the squamous label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A thin sheet composed of flattened cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which drawing carries this label?
teacher_understanding.answer: The uppermost, very thin epithelial drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a floor-tile image useful here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tiles suggest broad, flat units placed side by side, helping distinguish squamous cells from cubes or pillars.

p003-i7.exam_note: Identify squamous by flattened cells, not by a compulsory number of layers.

unpack.example_or_place: The table places simple squamous tissue in lung air sacs.
unpack.consequence: Connect a flat cell shape with the thin exchange layer discussed below.
unpack.visual_verb: Flatten a cell into a tile.
unpack.level_extra: Squamous names shape; simple or stratified names layering.

p003-i8.content: (b) Stratified squamous — points to the thick block with many cell layers and flattened cells at the exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: A multilayered epithelium whose upper cells are flattened.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature separates it from the top drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The visibly stacked layers rather than one thin sheet.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are many layers useful on a worn surface?
teacher_understanding.answer: Surface cells can be lost while deeper layers continue to cover the underlying tissue.

p003-i8.exam_note: Name stratified epithelium by the surface cells, not necessarily by basal cell shape.

unpack.example_or_place: Mouth lining, listed in the table.
unpack.consequence: Multiple layers support protection despite surface wear.
unpack.visual_verb: Stack layers and highlight the flat top.
unpack.level_extra: A columnar lower layer does not make this stratified columnar tissue.

p003-i9.content: (c) Cuboidal — points to the single layer of cube-like epithelial cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What shape does cuboidal describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing shows cells with a roughly cube-like form rather than flattened or tall slender cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which image is cuboidal?
teacher_understanding.answer: The third drawing, showing a single row of relatively short, block-like cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a learner avoid confusing cuboidal with columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: Compare height with width: cuboidal cells are approximately as tall as wide, whereas columnar cells are noticeably taller.

p003-i9.exam_note: Recognise the cube-like form despite the table's imprecise 'short cylindrical' wording.

unpack.example_or_place: Kidney tubules in the table.
unpack.consequence: Use shape recognition to connect the drawing to the cuboidal table row.
unpack.visual_verb: Compare a cube with a tall pillar.
unpack.level_extra: Approximate proportions matter; real cells need not be perfect geometric cubes.

p003-i10.content: (d) Columnar (Ciliated) — points to tall epithelial cells with a fringe of cilia on the exposed upper surface.

teacher_understanding.question: What two features does this label combine?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tall column-like cells and cilia at their exposed surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature indicates ciliated rather than merely columnar epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: The visible fringe of projections above the tall cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How do cilia assist surface movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Coordinated beating of these projections can move material along the epithelial surface.

p003-i10.exam_note: Cilia are a surface specialisation, not a separate layer of cells.

unpack.consequence: Cell shape and surface specialisation must be read as separate features.

unpack.level_extra: Do not infer that every columnar epithelium is ciliated.

p003-i11.content: Fig. 6.9: Different types of epithelial tissues
p003-i11.exam_note: Figure identifier only; content is captured in the diagram and labels.

p003-i12.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue | Location | Structure | Function
p003-i12.exam_note: Six epithelial types are organised by location, structure and function; each row is captured below.

p003-i13.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Simple squamous | Location: Blood vessel lining, capillaries, air sac lining of lungs, Bowman’s capsule of kidney | Structure: A single layer of flat cells having irregular boundaries | Function: Transport by diffusion and where minimal protection is required

teacher_understanding.question: What defines simple squamous structure?
teacher_understanding.answer: One layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries produces a thin epithelial sheet.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the table locate it?
teacher_understanding.answer: In blood vessel lining and capillaries, the air sac lining of lungs and Bowman’s capsule of the kidney.

teacher_understanding.question: Which function is associated with this arrangement?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates it with transport by diffusion and sites needing minimal protection.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a single flat layer suited to diffusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Exchange needs a short crossing distance. A thin single layer reduces that distance compared with a thick stack of cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from stratified squamous epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple squamous has one flat layer and is associated here with diffusion; stratified squamous has several layers and is associated with protection.

teacher_understanding.question: Should every listed location be taken to perform only diffusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. For example, the specialised lining associated with Bowman’s capsule participates in filtration. The table's broad diffusion entry should not erase location-specific functions.

p003-i13.exam_note: High-yield location matching; distinguish diffusion-friendly thinness from multilayer protection.

terms.everyday_image: फर्श पर टाइलों की एक पतली तह

why_chain.step: Exchange surfaces need substances to cross a short distance.
A single flattened cell layer provides a thin crossing barrier.

unpack.example_or_place: Zoom from breathing lungs to the air sac lining; also locate capillaries and the kidney capsule.
unpack.consequence: Thinness suits exchange, whereas stronger wear protection is associated later with many layers.
unpack.visual_verb: Pass particles across one flattened layer.
unpack.level_extra: Do not equate all renal epithelial structures with the same type or function.

p003-i14.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Simple Cuboidal Epithelium | Location: The tubular lining of kidneys, glandular ducts | Structure: A single layer of short cylindrical cells. It may have microvilli as in proximal convoluted tubules | Function: Absorption and secretion

teacher_understanding.question: What structure does the book assign to simple cuboidal epithelium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes a single layer of short cylindrical cells, sometimes with microvilli, as in proximal convoluted tubules.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is it found according to the table?
teacher_understanding.answer: In kidney tubular lining and glandular ducts.

teacher_understanding.question: What functions are linked to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Absorption and secretion: taking substances in and releasing substances are the two activities listed.

teacher_understanding.question: How do microvilli help an absorptive surface?
teacher_understanding.answer: These small surface projections enlarge the membrane area available for absorption without requiring a much larger organ.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the shape wording be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cuboidal conventionally means approximately as tall as wide. The printed phrase 'short cylindrical' is imprecise and should not be confused with tall columnar cells.

p003-i14.exam_note: Match kidney tubules and glandular ducts with simple cuboidal; microvilli increase absorption area, unlike motile cilia.

why_chain.step: Kidney tubules need to recover useful substances from the fluid passing through them.
Microvilli enlarge the absorptive surface of suitable tubular cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Zoom from the kidney to its small tubules; the proximal convoluted tubule is the microvilli example.
unpack.consequence: Surface modifications can enhance a tissue's function without changing its single-layer arrangement.
unpack.visual_verb: Enlarge a cell surface into microvilli and move substances across it.
unpack.level_extra: The book says 'may have': do not assign microvilli to every cuboidal epithelium.

p003-i15.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Simple Columnar Epithelium | Location: Digestive tract and upper respiratory tract lining | Structure: A single layer of columnar cells (tall and slender) and often ciliated | Function: Protection, absorption, mucus secretion and movement in a specific direction

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement does simple columnar describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: A single layer of tall, slender cells; the table also notes that they are often ciliated.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations does this row give?
teacher_understanding.answer: Digestive tract and upper respiratory tract lining.

teacher_understanding.question: What jobs does the row associate with these cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Protection, absorption, mucus secretion and movement in a specific direction.

teacher_understanding.question: How are mucus secretion and ciliary movement different jobs?
teacher_understanding.answer: Secretory cells release mucus, whereas beating cilia can move mucus and trapped material along a surface. Producing the material and moving it are distinct activities.

teacher_understanding.question: Should this row mean the entire upper respiratory tract is simple columnar?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Much of the conducting respiratory tract has pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, and some regions have other linings. The location entry is a broad simplification.

teacher_understanding.question: Are cilia and microvilli interchangeable?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Motile cilia move material along a surface, whereas microvilli primarily increase surface area for absorption.

p003-i15.exam_note: Distinguish tall shape, one layer and ciliation; avoid assuming every location performs every listed function.

why_chain.step: Internal passages need protection and handling of substances at their surfaces.
Columnar epithelial specialisations support absorption, secretion or directed surface movement according to the site.

unpack.example_or_place: Link digestive lining with taking in nutrients and respiratory cilia with moving mucus.
unpack.consequence: Cell shape alone does not specify every function; surface specialisation and location matter.
unpack.visual_verb: Raise tall cells, release mucus and sweep it in one direction.
unpack.level_extra: Treat the respiratory location cautiously; the next-page context introduces pseudostratified columnar epithelium.

p003-i16.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Stratified Squamous Epithelium | Location: The lining of the mouth and vagina | Structure: Made up of several layers of cells, continuously sloughed off and regenerated. The older layer of cells is pushed upwards and becomes flat. The lower layer is columnar and metabolically active | Function: Protection

teacher_understanding.question: What structural pattern defines this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several cell layers lie above a metabolically active columnar lower layer; older cells move upward and flatten.

teacher_understanding.question: Which locations are named?
teacher_understanding.answer: The mouth lining and vaginal lining.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page describe maintenance of the layers?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells are continuously sloughed off and regenerated, while older cells are pushed upward and become flat.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is renewal useful for a protective lining?
teacher_understanding.answer: Friction can remove exposed cells. Replacing them from deeper layers maintains a covering despite repeated wear.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a columnar basal layer not contradict the squamous name?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stratified epithelia are named according to the surface cell shape; the deeper cells can have a different shape.

p003-i16.exam_note: Strong location–protection match. Trap: basal cells are columnar but the superficial cells determine the squamous name.

terms.everyday_image: नीचे चलती हुई काम की कार्यशाला

why_chain.step: A lining exposed to repeated friction needs ongoing protection.
Several layers plus continual replacement preserve coverage as surface cells are lost.

unpack.example_or_place: The inside of the mouth experiences friction while food is chewed; vagina is the second listed site.
unpack.consequence: Protection is maintained by layered renewal rather than by the thin exchange design of simple squamous tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: Push cells upward, flatten them and shed the surface.
unpack.level_extra: Do not substitute skin for the page's stated examples; mouth and vagina are the listed locations.

p003-i17.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Stratified Cuboidal | Location: Mammary glands, sweat gland and salivary glands | Structure: The upper layer is cuboid and other layers may be cuboidal or other types | Function: Protection of ducts of various glands

teacher_understanding.question: What structural feature gives stratified cuboidal its name?
teacher_understanding.answer: The upper layer is cuboid; deeper layers may also be cuboidal or may have other cell types.

teacher_understanding.question: Which glands are named in the location column?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mammary glands, sweat gland and salivary glands; the function column specifically identifies protection of gland ducts.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are duct linings relevant to this protective role?
teacher_understanding.answer: A duct carries gland products along a passage. Multiple epithelial layers can provide a more substantial protective lining than a single thin exchange layer.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from simple cuboidal in the table?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple cuboidal has one layer and is associated with absorption and secretion; stratified cuboidal has multiple layers and is associated here with duct protection.

p003-i17.exam_note: Match stratified cuboidal with gland duct protection; do not infer that an entire gland has one epithelial type.

terms.everyday_image: शिशु को दूध पिलाना

why_chain.step: Gland products need a lined passage to travel through.
Stratified cuboidal tissue is linked here with protection of such ducts.

unpack.example_or_place: Sweat-gland ducts connect a familiar sweating experience with a protected gland passage.
unpack.consequence: Layer number distinguishes protective duct lining from simple cuboidal absorptive or secretory lining.
unpack.visual_verb: Line a gland duct with stacked cube-like cells.
unpack.level_extra: Location wording names glands broadly; keep attention on ducts rather than all secretory cells.

p003-i18.content: Types of Epithelial Tissue: Stratified Columnar | Location: Male urethra and lobar ducts of salivary glands | Structure: There is a layer of columnar cells present on squamous, columnar or cuboidal epithelial cells | Function: Protection and secretion

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement defines this row?
teacher_understanding.answer: A columnar cell layer lies over epithelial cells that may be squamous, columnar or cuboidal.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the page locate stratified columnar tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: In the male urethra and lobar ducts of salivary glands.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Protection and secretion.

teacher_understanding.question: How can deeper cells of different shapes still belong to stratified columnar tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The surface cells provide the shape term in the name, while 'stratified' records that more than one layer is present.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from stratified cuboidal?
teacher_understanding.answer: The upper layer is columnar rather than cuboid; the table associates stratified columnar with both protection and secretion, and stratified cuboidal with duct protection.

p003-i18.exam_note: Location matching and surface-cell naming are important. Do not confuse urethra with ureter or assume the whole urethra has one lining.

why_chain.step: Some passages need a protective lining with secretory activity.
The table associates these jobs with stratified tissue having a columnar surface layer.

unpack.example_or_place: Trace saliva from the familiar salivary gland into its larger ducts; also locate the male urethra as an exit passage.
unpack.consequence: The six rows can be organised using two independent criteria: number of layers and surface cell shape.
unpack.visual_verb: Place tall cells on a deeper layer and trace a duct.
